definition_zh: 使疏远；使不友好；离间；（法律）转让（财产、权利）
definition_en: to make someone who was friendly or loyal become cold or hostile; in law, to transfer property or a right to another person
core_image: 把原本属于自己的人推到门外去
scene: 他一句玩笑得罪了半个团队，从此没人愿意跟他搭档。 His sarcasm began to alienate his closest colleagues.
sceneCN: 这里 alienate 是「使疏远」（第 1 个义项：让人从亲近转为冷淡或敌对）；句意为他的讥讽开始让最亲近的同事疏远他。核心画面是把原本属于自己的人推到门外去。

pos.zh: 使疏远；使不友好；离间；转让

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成，义为「疏远；异化」
过去分词作形容词，义为「感到被疏远的」
同根形容词，义为「外国的；陌生的」

senses.title: To turn closeness into distance
senses.definition: to make someone who was friendly or loyal become cold, hostile or withdrawn, usually by your own behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 让原本友好或忠诚的人变得冷淡、敌对或退缩，通常由自己的行为造成
senses.example: The new rules alienated the very staff they were meant to help.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定反而让本该受照顾的员工疏远了。
senses.why: Alien means belonging to another, so alienate is to make someone into an outsider: you push a person who was yours across the boundary.
senses.whyCN: alien 意为「属于别人的」，所以 alienate 就是把某人变成外人：你把原本属于自己的人推过了界线。

senses.title: To transfer ownership away
senses.definition: in law, to transfer property or a right to another person, the older and technical sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产或权利转移给他人，是该词更古老、更专业的用法
senses.example: The trust forbids the heir to alienate the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 信托禁止继承人转让这份地产。
senses.why: This is the literal core: to make a thing alien, that is, the property of someone else, which is exactly what a legal transfer does.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：让某物变成 alien「别人的」，而法律上的转让做的正是这件事。

intro.en: Alienate comes straight from Latin alienus, belonging to another: to alienate is to make someone or something into the property of another, whether the loyalty of a friend or a piece of land.
intro.cn: alienate 直接来自拉丁语 alienus「属于别人的」：alienate 就是把某人或某物变成别人的，无论是朋友的忠诚还是一块土地。

items.en: Latin alius meant other or another, the root behind alias, alibi and alter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alius 意为「其他、另一个」，是 alias、alibi 与 alter 背后的词根。

items.en: From alius came alienus, belonging to another person, hence foreign or strange.
items.cn: 由 alius 派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，因此引申为外国的、陌生的。

items.en: The verb alienare meant to transfer ownership, and also to estrange the affection of a person.
items.cn: 动词 alienare 意为转移所有权，也指使人的感情疏远。

items.en: Its past participle alienatus carried both senses, legal transfer and emotional estrangement.
items.cn: 其过去分词 alienatus 同时承载两义：法律转让与感情疏远。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fourteenth century, first in law and soon after in descriptions of friendship.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入该词，先用于法律，随后用于描述友情。

items.en: Modern use favours the emotional sense, while the legal sense survives in deeds and in the noun alienation.
items.cn: 现代用法偏重感情义，法律义则保留在契据与名词 alienation 中。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ali- family of otherness; the near-meaning group lists other verbs for pushing people away.
note.cn: 形近组保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「把人推开」的动词。

entries.definition: Belonging to another place or person.
The state of being isolated or estranged.
A false or alternative name.
A claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred.
entries.definitionCN: 声称案发时身在别处的说法。

entries.definition: To cause someone to become unfriendly.
To keep yourself apart from someone.
entries.definitionCN: 让自己与某人保持距离。

entries.definition: To leave someone alone and unsupported.
To make someone lose loyalty.

normalIntro.en: Alienate is alien plus -ate: to make someone alien, an outsider, to you.
normalIntro.cn: alienate 就是 alien 加 -ate：把某人变成 alien，即变成你的外人。

normal.en: Alien means other, so alienate means to make other: the friend becomes a stranger.
normal.cn: alien 意为「他者」，所以 alienate 就是「使他者化」：朋友变成了陌生人。

normal.en: -ate turns the adjective into a verb, as in activate and isolate.
normal.cn: -ate 把形容词变成动词，如 activate、isolate。

normal.en: You alienate someone by your behaviour; you feel alienated by theirs.
normal.cn: 你的行为让别人疏远你；别人的行为让你感到被疏远。

normal.en: In law alienate simply means transfer, so alienate property is sell or give it away.
normal.cn: 法律上 alienate 就是转让，所以 alienate property 是卖掉或送出财产。

normal.en: The noun is alienation, not alienment: remember the -ation ending.
normal.cn: 名词是 alienation，不是 alienment：记住 -ation 这个词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a friend stepping across a line drawn on the floor and not coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个朋友跨过地上画的一条线，再也没有回来。

abstract.en: Imagine a door closing slowly between two people who used to share a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在两个曾同住一屋的人之间缓缓关上。

abstract.en: Think of a deed handing your land to the name of a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸契据把你的土地转到一个陌生人名下。

examples.en: Constant criticism will alienate even your supporters.
examples.cn: 不断的批评连你的支持者也会疏远。

examples.en: She felt alienated by the office gossip.
examples.cn: 办公室的闲言碎语让她感到被疏远。

examples.en: The clause prevents the owner from alienating the land.
examples.cn: 该条款阻止业主转让这块土地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶里诶内特」——诶（a）里（li）诶（e）内特（nate）：把里面的人推到外面去，就是使疏远、离间。

root: 拉丁语 alius「其他」派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，加动词后缀构成 alienare「转让、使疏远」，其过去分词 alienatus 经中古英语 alienaten 进入现代英语成为 alienate，字面即「使成为他者」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses move something across a boundary: the emotional one pushes a person out of your circle, and the legal one pushes a property out of your name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是把某样东西推过界线：感情义把人推出你的圈子，法律义把财产推出你的名下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pushing what was yours across the boundary
core.cn: 核心意象：把原本属于你的推过界线

branches.en: A joke that costs you a friend.
branches.cn: 一个让你失去朋友的玩笑。

branches.en: Rules that push loyal staff away.
branches.cn: 把忠诚员工推开的规定。

branches.en: A deed that moves land to a new name.
branches.cn: 把土地转到新名下的契据。

branches.en: A right signed over to another party.
branches.cn: 签字让给另一方的权利。

branches.en: Both make what was yours into the property of another.
branches.cn: 两者都把原本属于你的变成别人的。

intro.en: Alienate keeps the ali- root of otherness and adds -ate to make a verb, with -ation available for the resulting state.
intro.cn: alienate 保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词根，加 -ate 构成动词，并可用 -ation 表示由此产生的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius gave alienus, alienare and alienatus; English took the participle and kept both of its senses.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 派生出 alienus、alienare 与 alienatus；英语取用其分词，并保留了它的两个义项。

latinEntries.example: Alius is the root of the ali- family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alius 是 ali- 词族的词根。
alienus 产生 alien 与 alienate。

latinEntries.example: Alienatus is the direct source of alienate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alienatus 是 alienate 的直接来源。

definition_zh: adj. 可以达到的；能够获得的（目标、水平、结果）
definition_en: Able to be reached, achieved or obtained, especially of a goal or standard that is realistic.
core_image: 伸手就能碰到的那根横杆
scene: 教练把跳高横杆降到学生平时能过的高度，说这样目标才有意义。 The coach lowered the bar to a height that was attainable for every student.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attainable 指目标在能力范围之内，努力之后确实能够达到。

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

derivatives.zh: 达到；获得
成就；达到
无法达到的
可达到性

senses.title: A goal within reach
senses.definition: of an aim, level or result that a person can realistically reach with effort
senses.definitionCN: 指目标、水平或结果在努力之后确实能够达到
senses.example: She set an attainable target of ten pages a day.
senses.exampleCN: 她定了每天十页这个可达成的目标。
senses.why: The word joins attain, to reach, with -able, capable of, so it literally means reachable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 attain「达到」加 -able「能够……的」构成，字面就是「可达到的」。

senses.title: Available to be obtained
senses.definition: of a resource, status or benefit that can actually be got or secured
senses.definitionCN: 指资源、地位或利益实际上可以取得或获得
senses.example: Free childcare is attainable only in a few districts.
senses.exampleCN: 免费托育只在少数几个区才能获得。
senses.why: Once reaching a height was clear, the same suffix pattern covered getting hold of anything desired.
senses.whyCN: 「达到某个高度」清楚之后，同一后缀模式也覆盖了「取得任何想要的东西」。

intro.en: Attainable is attain plus -able; attain comes from Old French ataindre, from Latin attingere, to touch upon, from ad-, to, and tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: attainable 是 attain 加 -able；attain 来自古法语 ataindre，出自拉丁语 attingere「触及」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成。

items.en: The root tag- meant to touch, the physical act behind a whole family of contact words.
items.cn: 词根 tag- 意为「触碰」，是一整族接触类词背后的身体动作。

items.en: Latin tangere meant to touch, giving tangent, contact and contingent.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 意为「触」，产生 tangent、contact 与 contingent。

items.en: With ad-, to, added, attingere meant to touch upon, to reach as far as a point.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」，attingere 意为「触及」，即延伸到某一点。

items.en: Old French ataindre kept the sense of reaching a place or a person.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre 保留了「抵达某地或某人」的意思。

items.en: Middle English atteynen meant to reach or arrive at, later spelled attain.
items.cn: 中古英语 atteynen 意为「达到、抵达」，后来拼作 attain。

items.en: English added -able in the sixteenth century to say that a goal could be reached.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪加上 -able，用来表示某个目标能够达到。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the attain family and one familiar -able word; the near-meaning group lists other words for a goal that can be met.
note.cn: 形近组保留 attain 词族和一个常见的 -able 词；近义组列出其他表示目标能够达成的词。

entries.definition: To reach or achieve something.
Impossible to reach.
The quality of being reachable.
Able to be kept up over time.
Able to be accomplished.
Possible to do in practice.
Sensible given the limits.
Able to be got to.

normalIntro.en: Attainable splits into attain plus -able: if you can attain it, it is attainable.
normalIntro.cn: attainable 拆成 attain 加 -able：能达到的，就是 attainable。

normal.en: Attain means reach; -able means can be.
normal.cn: attain 意为达到，-able 意为「可以被」。

normal.en: The opposite adds un-: unattainable.
normal.cn: 反义加 un- 就成 unattainable。

normal.en: Goals should be challenging yet attainable.
normal.cn: 目标应当有挑战但仍可达成。

normal.en: The noun is attainability, not attainableness.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 attainability，不用 attainableness。

normal.en: It usually sits before goal, target or standard.
normal.cn: 它通常放在 goal、target 或 standard 之前。

abstract.en: Picture a high-jump bar set at your own height.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高横杆设在你自己能够的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a shelf just within your fingertips.
abstract.cn: 想象一层刚好在指尖之内的架子。

abstract.en: Think of a plan whose last step is possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一份最后一步确实可行的计划。

examples.en: The salary is attainable after two years.
examples.cn: 两年后这份薪水是可以拿到的。

examples.en: Make the first milestone easily attainable.
examples.cn: 把第一个里程碑定得容易达到。

examples.en: Such purity is not attainable at home.
examples.cn: 这样的纯度在家无法达到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：attain「达到」+ -able「可以……的」——能够达到的，就是 attainable。

root: 拉丁语 tangere「触」加 ad-「向」成 attingere「触及」，经古法语 ataindre 入英语作 attain「达到」；再加 -able 表「可以被达到」，即 attainable。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same reach: a height you can get to, and a thing you can get hold of.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种「够得到」：能达到的高度，以及能拿到手的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar set just within the reach of your hand
core.cn: 核心意象：横杆设在伸手就能碰到的高度

branches.en: A daily page target one can meet.
branches.cn: 能完成的每日页数目标。

branches.en: A bar lowered to a reachable height.
branches.cn: 降到可及高度的横杆。

branches.en: Free childcare only in a few districts.
branches.cn: 只在少数区能获得的免费托育。

branches.en: A salary one can earn in two years.
branches.cn: 两年内能挣到的薪水。

branches.en: Both stay inside real limits.
branches.cn: 两者都在现实限制之内。

intro.en: Attainable is at- plus tain plus -able; the same tain root builds contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: attainable 是 at- 加 tain 加 -able；同一 tain 词根还构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is tangere, to touch, and attingere, to touch upon; tenere, to hold, gives the look-alike tain family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 tangere「触」与 attingere「触及」；tenere「持」则给出形近的 tain 词族。

definition_zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的
definition_en: relating to earthquakes or to the vibrations they send through the ground
core_image: 一条波线从地底某一点向四面扩散，经过之处墙体和地表都在轻微起伏
scene: 地震台网的值班室里，屏幕上一条波形刚刚越过警戒线。 Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 seismic 是「地震的」（第 1 个义项：与地震或地震引起的震动有关）；句意为谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。

pos.zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的

derivatives.zh: 地震活动性；某地区的地震频度
无地震的；抗震的
地震现象（少用）
在地震方面；按抗震方式
地震学（seismo- 组合形式参与构成的学科名）

senses.title: Relating to earthquakes
senses.definition: connected with earthquakes or with the shaking of the earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 与地震或地壳震动相关的
senses.example: Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。
senses.why: seismic comes from Greek seismos, a shaking or earthquake, so the adjective simply points to that event.
senses.whyCN: seismic 来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，因此这个形容词直接指向那个事件。

senses.title: Concerning seismic waves
senses.definition: describing the elastic waves that travel through rock after a sudden rupture
senses.definitionCN: 描述岩体突然破裂后在岩石中传播的弹性波
senses.example: Seismic waves arrive from the focus in several distinct phases.
senses.exampleCN: 地震波以几个不同震相从震源抵达。
senses.why: once instruments could record the shaking, the adjective was attached to the waves that carry it, not only to the event.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能记录震动之后，这个形容词就不仅指事件，也用于承载震动的波。

senses.title: Monitoring ground motion
senses.definition: used for instruments, networks or data that detect and measure ground shaking
senses.definitionCN: 用于探测与测量地面震动的仪器、台网或数据
senses.example: The seismic network sent an alert before the strongest shaking arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 地震台网在最强震动到达前发出了警报。
senses.why: a monitoring system is named by what it watches, so seismic became the standard label for earthquake detection.
senses.whyCN: 监测系统按它监视的对象命名，因此 seismic 成了地震探测的标准标签。

senses.title: Imaging the ground by sound
senses.definition: relating to the method that sends artificial vibrations into the ground and reads their echoes
senses.definitionCN: 与向地下发送人工震动并读取回波的方法有关
senses.example: A seismic survey mapped the salt dome under the seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 一次地震勘探测出了海床下的盐丘。
senses.why: the same physics that records earthquakes can be reversed: make a controlled shock and listen to the reflections.
senses.whyCN: 记录地震的同一套物理可以反用：制造可控震动，再听反射。

senses.title: Based on seismic data
senses.definition: derived from recorded ground motion, as in images of rock layers or fault maps
senses.definitionCN: 由记录到的地面运动推得，如岩层图像或断层图
senses.example: The seismic image shows a buried fault beneath the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 地震图像显示三角洲下有一条被掩埋的断层。
senses.why: data is named by the physical signal that produced it, so seismic became a shorthand for the whole imaging method.
senses.whyCN: 数据按产生它的物理信号命名，因此 seismic 成了整套成像方法的简称。

senses.title: Relating to earthquake risk
senses.definition: concerning the probability and expected strength of shaking at a place
senses.definitionCN: 关于某地发生震动的概率与预期强度
senses.example: The building code sets seismic requirements for every new school.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑规范为每所新建学校规定了抗震要求。
senses.why: risk language uses the adjective because the hazard itself is the shaking, not the fault line on a map.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言使用这个形容词，因为危险本身是震动，而不是地图上的断层线。

senses.title: Designed to resist earthquakes
senses.definition: built or fitted so that structures can survive strong shaking
senses.definitionCN: 为使结构能在强烈震动中存留而建造或装配
senses.example: Seismic isolation lets the base move while the floors stay steady.
senses.exampleCN: 地震隔震让底座移动而楼层保持稳定。
senses.why: engineering turns the adjective into a design goal: whatever resists the shaking is called seismic.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把这个形容词变成设计目标：凡是能抵御震动的都冠以 seismic。

senses.title: Figuratively enormous in effect
senses.titleCN: 比喻：影响如同地震般巨大的
senses.definition: having an effect as sudden and far-reaching as an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 产生的影响如地震般突然而深远
senses.example: The ruling caused a seismic shift in how the industry was financed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决使该行业的融资方式发生了地震般的转变。
senses.why: the figurative sense borrows the scale of an earthquake: not just a change, but one that rearranges the ground under everything.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了地震的规模：不只是变化，而是把一切脚下的地面重新排布。

intro.en: Seismic was formed in English in the nineteenth century from Greek seismos, a shaking, an earthquake, built on the verb seiein, to shake, plus the adjective suffix -ic. It has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: seismic 是 19 世纪英语新造词，来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，其词根为动词 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic。它没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Seiein meant to shake or drive by shaking. Its deeper pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: seiein 意为「摇动、以摇动驱使」。其希腊语之前的更深来源未获证明，因此为它给出的任何印欧形式都属重构。

items.en: Seismos named a shaking or an earthquake; the same stem appears in seismology and in older medical use for trembling.
items.cn: seismos 指一次震动或地震；同一词干也出现在 seismology，以及较早医学用语中的「颤抖」。

items.en: English scientists coined seismic in the mid nineteenth century to name the study and measurement of earthquakes, at a time when seismology was becoming a science.
items.cn: 19 世纪中叶，英语科学界造出 seismic，用来命名地震的研究与测量，当时地震学正成为一门科学。

items.en: In the twentieth century seismic survey came to mean deliberate sound-wave imaging of rock layers for oil, gas and engineering.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，seismic survey 指为石油、天然气与工程目的，用声波对岩层做主动成像。

items.en: Late modern English extended the adjective to any change of earthquake scale, as in a seismic shift in policy or markets.
items.cn: 现代英语晚期把这个形容词扩展到任何地震级的变化，如政策或市场上的地震式转变。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek root of seiein is unsettled, and the earliest printed use of seismic is dated only approximately to the 1850s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：seiein 的希腊语之前词根尚无定论，seismic 最早的印刷用例也只能约略定在 1850 年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek shaking stem; group two holds adjectives that describe large earth movements or huge effects.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「震动」词干的词；第二组是描述大规模地壳运动或巨大影响的形容词。

entries.definition: An older synonym meaning relating to an earthquake; it is now rare beside seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的同义词，意为「与地震有关的」；如今除 seismic 外已罕用。

entries.definition: Built with the Greek negative prefix a-: either free from earthquakes or designed to resist them.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊否定前缀 a- 构成：或指无地震的，或指抗震的。

entries.definition: The frequency and distribution of earthquakes in a region; the noun behind seismic activity.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区地震的频度与分布；即 seismic activity 背后的名词。

entries.definition: Seismo- plus -graph, a writing instrument: the device that draws a record of ground motion.
entries.definitionCN: seismo- 加 -graph「书写」：把地面运动画成记录曲线的仪器。

entries.definition: Relating to the structure of the earth's crust and the plates that move it; tectonic events cause earthquakes but the word does not mean seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳结构及推动地壳的板块有关；构造事件会引发地震，但该词本身并不等于 seismic。

entries.definition: Literally shaking the earth, but in practice almost always figurative for enormously important; seismic covers both the literal and figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 字面为「摇动大地」，实际几乎总作比喻指「极其重大」；seismic 则兼具字面与比喻两义。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of the earth as a whole, including gravity, magnetism and heat; seismic is only one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地球的物理有关，包括重力、磁场与热；seismic 只是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: Describing a disastrous outcome; it can describe an earthquake's effects but says nothing about shaking as such.
entries.definitionCN: 描述灾难性后果；可描述地震的影响，但本身并不指震动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek seismos, shaking, plus -ic: the adjective of an earthquake.
normal.cn: 希腊 seismos「震动」加 -ic：地震的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs seismic, seismicity, aseismic, seismograph, seismometer, seismogram, seismology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 seismic、seismicity、aseismic、seismograph、seismometer、seismogram、seismology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seismic wave, seismic survey, seismic hazard, seismic design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地震波、地震勘探、地震危险、抗震设计。

normal.en: seismo- is the combining form in instrument names, always tied to ground motion.
normal.cn: seismo- 是仪器名称中的组合形式，始终与地面运动相关。

normal.en: The figurative phrase seismic shift is a set expression for a very large change.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配 seismic shift 是「巨大转变」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in a pond, but the rings run through rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落入池塘，只是涟漪穿过的是岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a city where every table starts sliding at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市里每张桌子在同一瞬间开始滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook rewritten overnight while everyone is still asleep.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册在众人熟睡时被一夜改写。

examples.en: The region has been quiet, with no seismic activity for a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区一直平静，十年来没有地震活动。

examples.en: Seismic reflection revealed a deep basin beneath the plain.
examples.cn: 地震反射探测揭示出平原之下有一个深盆地。

examples.en: The new evidence caused a seismic change in the accepted theory.
examples.cn: 新证据使公认理论发生了地震般的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seis（震）+ mic」——大地在抖动 → 地震的、震动的

root: 希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，源自 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic；希腊来源，无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same shaking: first the earthquake itself, then its waves, its monitoring, its use for imaging, its data, its risk, its engineering answer, and finally any change on the same scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种震动展开：先是地震本身，继而它的波、监测、成像用途、数据、风险、工程对策，最后是任何同等规模的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave front spreading from one point underground, tilting everything it passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道波前从地下某点扩散，经过之处一切都在倾斜。

branches.en: THE EVENT: seismic points first at the earthquake itself.
branches.cn: 事件：seismic 首先指向地震本身。

branches.en: CARRYING AND WATCHING: waves carry the shaking, instruments watch it.
branches.cn: 承载与监视：波承载震动，仪器监视震动。

branches.en: ACTIVE USE: the same physics is turned into a lamp for the subsurface.
branches.cn: 主动利用：同一套物理被改造为照亮地下的灯。

branches.en: RISK AND RESPONSE: shaking becomes a design load to be resisted.
branches.cn: 风险与应对：震动变成必须抵御的设计荷载。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the scale of an earthquake is lent to social change.
branches.cn: 比喻：把地震的规模借给社会变化。

intro.en: Seismic is a Greek-derived adjective whose combining form seismo- appears at the front of a whole family of earth-science words.
intro.cn: seismic 是希腊来源的形容词，其组合形式 seismo- 出现在整族地球科学词汇的词首。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the family goes back to Greek seiein and seismos, and Latin gained only loanwords such as the medical use of tremor.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先：这个词族上溯希腊 seiein 与 seismos；拉丁语只贡献了如医学用法的 tremor 等借词。

items.example: Seismo- heads the names of instruments and sciences.
items.exampleCN: seismo- 位于仪器与学科名称的词首。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The verb supplies the root sei-.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词根 sei-。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.meaning: the earthquake frequency of a region
items.example: Low seismicity made the site attractive.
items.exampleCN: 地震活动性低使该场址颇具吸引力。

items.example: The seismograph traced a long, low pulse.
items.exampleCN: 地震仪描出一条长而低的脉冲。

items.meaning: an instrument that measures ground motion
the record produced by a seismograph
items.exampleCN: 地震记录图显示两个到达震相。

items.example: Seismology grew from early earthquake catalogues.
items.exampleCN: 地震学从早期地震目录发展而来。

definition_zh: 疏远；疏离感；（哲学）异化；（法律）转让
definition_en: the state of feeling isolated from people, work or society; in social theory, estrangement from your own labour; in law, the transfer of property
core_image: 站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃
scene: 搬进新城市半年，他每天上班打卡，却谁也不认识。 Alienation grew quietly behind his polite smile.
sceneCN: 这里 alienation 是「疏离感」（第 1 个义项：与周围人或环境失去联系的心理状态）；句意为疏离感在他礼貌的微笑背后悄悄滋长。核心画面是站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃。

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 的动词，义为「使疏远；转让」
过去分词作形容词，义为「感到被疏远的」
同根形容词，义为「外国的；陌生的」

senses.title: The feeling of being cut off
senses.definition: the state of feeling isolated from the people, work or society around you, as though a wall stood between you and them
senses.definitionCN: 感到与周围的人、工作或社会隔绝的状态，仿佛彼此之间立着一道墙
senses.example: Long shifts and empty weekends deepened his alienation.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的班次与空荡的周末加深了他的疏离感。
senses.why: Alien means other, and -ation names a state, so alienation is the state of having become other: you are among people yet no longer of them.
senses.whyCN: alien 意为「他者」，-ation 表示状态，所以 alienation 就是「已成为他者」的状态：你在人群之中，却不再属于他们。

senses.title: Loss of control over your own work
senses.definition: in social theory, the condition in which workers lose control over what they make and feel estranged from their own labour
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中，劳动者失去对自己产品的控制、并与自身劳动相疏离的状态
senses.example: Marx described alienation as the worker lost in the product.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思把异化描述为劳动者在自己的产品中失落。
senses.why: This sense narrows the general wall to one specific place: the workshop, where what you build no longer feels like yours.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把那堵普遍的墙收窄到一个具体场所：车间，你造出来的东西不再感觉属于你。

senses.title: The legal transfer of property
senses.definition: in law, the act of transferring ownership of property to another person, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产所有权转移给他人的行为，是该词最古老的用法
senses.example: The deed records the alienation of the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据记录了家族农场的转让。
senses.why: Here the word stays literal: making a thing alien means making it the property of someone else, which is precisely what a transfer does.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词保持字面义：让某物变成 alien「别人的」，正是转让所做的事。

intro.en: Alienation is the noun of alienate: Latin alienus, belonging to another, plus the process suffix -ation, naming the state of having been made other.
intro.cn: alienation 是 alienate 的名词形式：拉丁语 alienus「属于别人的」加过程后缀 -ation，表示「已被变成他者」的状态。

items.en: Latin alius meant other, the root of alias, alibi and alter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alius 意为「其他」，是 alias、alibi 与 alter 的词根。

items.en: Alienus meant belonging to another, and so foreign, strange or unrelated.
items.cn: alienus 意为「属于别人的」，因此引申为外国的、陌生的、无关的。

items.en: The noun alienatio named a transfer of ownership in Roman law, and also a loss of reason or affection.
items.cn: 名词 alienatio 在罗马法中指所有权转让，也指理智或感情的丧失。

items.en: Old French alienation kept the legal sense, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 alienation 保留法律义，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Philosophy and sociology widened the word in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to name estrangement from work and society.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，哲学与社会学拓宽该词，用以指与劳动和社会的疏离。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ali- family of otherness; the near-meaning group lists other words for feeling cut off.
note.cn: 形近组保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「感到隔绝」的词。

entries.definition: To make someone cold or hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人变得冷淡或敌对。

entries.definition: Belonging to another place or person.
Feeling isolated and unwanted.
A change made to something.
The state of being alone and separated.
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人与外界分离的状态。

entries.definition: The loss of affection between people.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间感情的丧失。

entries.definition: Sadness at being alone.
A break in a link or relationship.

normalIntro.en: Alienation is alienate plus -ion: the state produced when someone is made alien.
normalIntro.cn: alienation 就是 alienate 加 -ion：把某人变成外人之后产生的那种状态。

normal.en: Alienate is the verb, alienation the result: one pushes, the other is the distance left.
normal.cn: alienate 是动词，alienation 是结果：一个是推，一个是推完后留下的距离。

normal.en: Alien means other, so alienation is otherness turned into a feeling.
normal.cn: alien 意为「他者」，所以 alienation 就是「他者性」变成的一种感受。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say a sense of alienation, not an alienation.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 a sense of alienation，不说 an alienation。

normal.en: In sociology alienation from work is a fixed phrase; keep the from.
normal.cn: 社会学中 alienation from work 是固定搭配，别丢掉 from。

normal.en: In law the alienation of property simply means its transfer.
normal.cn: 法律上 the alienation of property 就是财产转让。

abstract.en: Picture standing in a crowded room behind a sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象站在拥挤的房间里，面前隔着一层玻璃。

abstract.en: Imagine building a chair all day and never being allowed to sit in it.
abstract.cn: 想象整天做椅子，却从不被允许坐上去。

abstract.en: Think of your own name written on a door you can no longer open.
abstract.cn: 想象你自己的名字写在一扇你再也打不开的门上。

examples.en: Alienation often follows a long move to a new city.
examples.cn: 搬到一个新城市后，疏离感常常随之而来。

examples.en: The survey measured alienation among night-shift workers.
examples.cn: 这项调查测量了夜班工人的疏离感。

examples.en: Any alienation of the land needs the consent of both heirs.
examples.cn: 这块土地的任何转让都需两位继承人同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶里诶内申」——诶里（alien）是外人，诶内申（ation）是状态：变成外人的那种状态，就是疏离、异化。

root: 拉丁语 alius「其他」派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，加动词后缀构成 alienare「转让、使疏远」，其名词 alienatio 经古法语 alienation 进入英语，字面即「被变成他者的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses describe the same crossing: a person becomes other to their community, a worker becomes other to their product, and a property becomes other to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项描述的是同一次跨越：人对自己的社群成为他者，劳动者对自己的产品成为他者，财产对原主成为他者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass wall between you and what was yours
core.cn: 核心意象：你与原本属于你的一切之间隔着一层玻璃

branches.en: A polite smile hiding no real contact.
branches.cn: 礼貌的微笑背后没有真正的接触。

branches.en: A new city where nobody knows your name.
branches.cn: 一座没人知道你名字的新城市。

branches.en: A worker who never owns what they build.
branches.cn: 从不拥有自己产品的劳动者。

branches.en: A deed moving land to another name.
branches.cn: 把土地转到别人名下的契据。

branches.en: All three make what was yours into the property of another.
branches.cn: 三者都把原本属于你的变成别人的。

intro.en: Alienation keeps the ali- root of otherness, the verb suffix -ate and the result suffix -ion, so the whole history is visible in the spelling.
intro.cn: alienation 保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词根、动词后缀 -ate 与结果后缀 -ion，整段历史都写在拼写里。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius gave alienus, alienare and the noun alienatio, which French passed to English with both senses intact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 派生出 alienus、alienare 与名词 alienatio，法语把它传给英语时两义都完好保留。

latinEntries.example: Alius is the root of ali-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: alius 是 ali- 的词根。

definition_zh: n. 双肩背包；背包；v. 背着背包旅行；徒步自助旅行
definition_en: A bag carried on the back by two shoulder straps; as a verb, to travel cheaply carrying such a bag.
core_image: 两条肩带把全部家当挂在背上
scene: 他把两天的衣物塞进背包就出门了。 He stuffed two days of clothes into his backpack and left.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：backpack 指用两条肩带背在背上的包。

derivatives.zh: 背包旅行者
背包自助旅行
打包；装填
登山背包

senses.title: A bag worn on the back
senses.definition: a bag with two shoulder straps, carried on the back to leave the hands free
senses.definitionCN: 带两条肩带、背在背上以腾出双手的包
senses.example: Her backpack held a tent and a stove.
senses.exampleCN: 她的背包里装着一顶帐篷和一个炉子。
senses.why: Backpack is back plus pack, so it names a load by where it is carried rather than by its shape.
senses.whyCN: backpack 是 back 加 pack，因此它用「背在哪里」而不是形状来命名这份负载。

senses.title: To travel with one
senses.definition: to travel cheaply and independently, carrying one’s belongings in such a bag
senses.definitionCN: 以背包携带行李，廉价而自主地旅行
senses.example: They backpacked across three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们背包走过三个国家。
senses.why: The bag came to stand for a whole style of travel, so the noun turned into a verb for that style.
senses.whyCN: 这种包代表了一整种旅行方式，于是名词转为表示该方式的动词。

intro.en: Backpack is back plus pack; pack came through Middle Dutch pakke, of uncertain origin, and the compound is recorded in American English in the 1910s.
intro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack；pack 经中古荷兰语 pakke 传入，来源不确定，这个复合词于 1910 年代在美式英语中有记载。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back, the surface that carries a load.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「背」，即承载负荷的那一面。

items.en: Middle Dutch pakke meant a bundle or bale, a word of trade rather than learning.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pakke 意为「捆、包」，是商贸用语而非学术词。

items.en: Middle English packe named a bundle carried by a person or an animal.
items.cn: 中古英语 packe 指由人或牲畜驮运的捆包。

items.en: American English formed backpack in the 1910s for a bag with shoulder straps.
items.cn: 美式英语在 1910 年代造出 backpack，指带肩带的包。

items.en: The verb meaning to travel with a backpack spread in the 1960s.
items.cn: 表示背包旅行的动词用法在 1960 年代流行开来。

items.en: The noun became standard for school bags and for hiking gear alike.
items.cn: 这个名词同时成为学生书包与徒步装备的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the pack family; the near-meaning group lists other bags and one word for the traveller.
note.cn: 形近组保留 pack 词族；近义组列出其他包袋与一个指旅行者的词。

entries.definition: A person who travels with a backpack.
A bundle, or to fill a bag.
A wrapped parcel.
To go back along a route.
A bag carried on the back.
A soldier’s or walker’s back bag.
A bag with a single long strap.
A stout bag for provisions.

normalIntro.en: Backpack is back plus pack: a bundle carried on the back, and then the whole style of travel built around it.
normalIntro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack：背在背上的捆包，进而指围绕它形成的整种旅行方式。

normal.en: Two straps make it a backpack.
normal.cn: 两条肩带才叫 backpack。

normal.en: Rucksack is the British cousin.
normal.cn: rucksack 是英式的近亲。

normal.en: The verb gives backpacked and backpacking.
normal.cn: 动词有 backpacked 与 backpacking。

normal.en: The traveller is a backpacker.
normal.cn: 旅行者是 backpacker。

normal.en: Backpack through a place is the pattern.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 backpack through 某地。

abstract.en: Picture your whole week hanging on two straps.
abstract.cn: 想象一整周的家当挂在两条带子上。

abstract.en: Imagine hands free on a mountain path.
abstract.cn: 想象山路上双手空着。

abstract.en: Think of a hostel bed booked that morning.
abstract.cn: 想象当天早上才订的青年旅舍床位。

examples.en: He left his backpack on the train.
examples.cn: 他把背包落在火车上了。

examples.en: They backpacked for six weeks.
examples.cn: 他们背包旅行了六周。

examples.en: The backpack straps dug into her shoulders.
examples.cn: 背包肩带勒进她的肩膀。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「背」+ pack「捆包」——背在背上的包就是 backpack；背上它去旅行，就是动词「背包游」。

root: 古英语 baec「背」加经中古荷兰语 pakke 传入的 pack「捆包」，1910 年代美式英语合成 backpack；1960 年代衍生动词「背包旅行」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one load on two straps: the bag itself, and the independent travel that the bag makes possible.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一份挂在两条带子上的负载：包本身，以及这种包使之可能的自主旅行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two shoulder straps holding everything you own on your back
core.cn: 核心意象：两条肩带把全部家当挂在背上

branches.en: Two days of clothes stuffed in.
branches.cn: 塞进两天衣物的包。

branches.en: A tent and a stove carried.
branches.cn: 带着的帐篷与炉子。

branches.en: Three countries crossed on foot.
branches.cn: 徒步走过的三个国家。

branches.en: Six weeks of cheap travel.
branches.cn: 六周的廉价旅行。

branches.en: The bag defines the way of going.
branches.cn: 这只包定义了出行方式。

intro.en: Backpack is back plus pack; -er makes the traveller, -ing the activity, and -age gives package from the same pack.
intro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack；-er 造出旅行者，-ing 造出活动，而 -age 由同一 pack 给出 package。

latinIntro.en: Pack is a trade word from Dutch rather than Latin; Latin sarcina, a bundle, gives the learned sarcina of botany beside it.
latinIntro.cn: pack 是来自荷兰语的商贸词而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 sarcina「捆包」给出植物学中的学术用词。

definition_zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；（公众）关注度
definition_en: the distance one can see clearly, or the state of being able to be seen
core_image: 从山脊望向远处，一层层山影越来越淡
scene: 清晨的山路上雾很重，前面的路牌要走近才看得清。 Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
sceneCN: 这里 visibility 是「能见度」（第 1 个义项：能看清的距离）；句意为大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。从山脊望出去、远山越来越淡的那幅画面，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 能见度；可见性；可见程度；关注度

collocations.phrase: raise the visibility of an issue
collocations.zh: 提高某个议题的关注度

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「可见的；明显的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不可见性」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: The distance one can see
senses.definition: the distance at which objects can be clearly seen, especially in weather reports
senses.definitionCN: 能清晰看见物体的距离，尤用于天气报告
senses.example: Fog cut visibility to less than fifty metres on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 大雾使高速路上的能见度降到不足五十米。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives vis-, and -ity names a quality, so visibility is literally the quality of being able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出 vis-，-ity 表示性质，所以 visibility 字面上就是「能被看见的程度」。

senses.title: The state of being seen
senses.definition: the fact or degree of something being able to be seen at all
senses.definitionCN: 某物能否被看见、被看见到什么程度
senses.example: The tall trees limited the visibility of the path from the house.
senses.exampleCN: 高树挡住了从屋里看到小路的视线。
senses.why: Strip the weather away and the word still measures how much a thing can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 去掉天气的成分，这个词仍在衡量一件事物能被看到多少。

senses.title: Public attention
senses.definition: the degree to which a person or a cause is noticed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一项事业被公众注意的程度
senses.example: The campaign gave the small charity national visibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动让那家小慈善机构获得全国关注。
senses.why: A cause that can be seen is a cause people can support, so being seen turned into being noticed publicly.
senses.whyCN: 看得见的事业才能得到支持，于是「被看见」变成了「被公众注意」。

senses.title: Clearness of a design or a text
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to see and read, in print or on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 印刷或屏幕上易于看见和阅读的程度
senses.example: Contrast improves the visibility of small text on a screen.
senses.exampleCN: 提高对比度可以改善屏幕上小字的清晰度。
senses.why: Typesetters and designers need the same quality as weather forecasters: how well a thing comes to the eye.
senses.whyCN: 排版者与设计师需要的品质和气象预报员一样：东西进入眼睛的效果有多好。

senses.title: The character of being plainly evident
senses.definition: the quality of something being obvious or clear to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 某事物对所有人都明显、清楚的性质
senses.example: The visibility of the mistake made the meeting awkward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误太显眼，让会议很尴尬。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be hidden, it is visible in a strong sense, and the noun names that plainness.
senses.whyCN: 若一件事藏不住，它就在强意义上可见，名词便指这种显而易见。

intro.en: Visibility comes from Latin videre, to see, through the adjective visibilis, able to be seen.
intro.cn: visibility 来自拉丁语 videre（看见），经由形容词 visibilis（能被看见的）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and the stem vis- carries that meaning into many English words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，词干 vis- 把这个意思带进许多英语词。

items.en: Visibilis was formed to mean able to be seen.
items.cn: visibilis 构造成「能被看见的」。

items.en: The abstract noun visibilitas named the quality of being seen.
items.cn: 抽象名词 visibilitas 指能被看见这一性质。

items.en: English took visibility in the sixteenth century, mainly in learned writing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 visibility，主要用于学术写作。

items.en: Aviation and motoring turned it into a measured distance in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪航空与汽车交通把它变成一个可测的距离。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the words for sight and for being noticed.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收视觉与被注意相关词。

entries.definition: The adjective, meaning able to be seen.
The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
The state of not being able to be seen.
Sight itself, or a picture seen in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 看的能力，或心中所见之景。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen.
The quality of being clear, in air, sound or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 空气、声音或文字清晰的性质。

entries.definition: Public attention given to a person or a product.
entries.definitionCN: 给予人或产品的公众注意。

entries.definition: The state of being important and noticed.

normalIntro.en: The see-root plus -ity: a quality of being seen, measured in metres by pilots and drivers.
normalIntro.cn: 「看」词根加 -ity：一种被看见的性质，又被飞行员与司机用米来量。

normal.en: Vis- means to see, from Latin videre.
normal.cn: vis- 意为看见，源自拉丁语 videre。

normal.en: -ity turns visible into a quality, as in ability and clarity.
normal.cn: -ity 把 visible 变成性质名词，如 ability、clarity。

normal.en: Visibility is uncountable: poor visibility, not a visibility.
normal.cn: visibility 不可数：说 poor visibility。

normal.en: In weather it is a distance; in public life it is attention.
normal.cn: 在天气里它是距离，在公共生活中它是关注。

normal.en: Invisibility is the opposite, formed with in-.
normal.cn: invisibility 是反面，用 in- 构成。

abstract.en: See ridges fading one behind the other into haze.
abstract.cn: 想象一道道山脊越远越淡，没入雾中。

abstract.en: Hear a radio voice giving the distance in metres.
abstract.cn: 听广播报出以米计的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that everyone in the street can read at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块全街人都能同时看清的牌子。

examples.en: Visibility was poor on the mountain road that morning.
examples.cn: 那天早上山路的能见度很差。

examples.en: The new logo increased the brand's visibility.
examples.cn: 新标志提高了品牌的曝光度。

examples.en: Thick glass reduced the visibility of the numbers.
examples.cn: 厚玻璃让数字变得看不清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为扎必了体」——雾太浓，为看清路得扎着脖子，能见度实在太低。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（可见的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 visibilitas → 英语 visibility；同根词有 visible、vision、advise。

sensesIntro.en: How well a thing comes to the eye becomes a measured distance, then a share of public attention, then a plainness nobody can miss.
sensesIntro.cn: 「东西进入眼睛的效果」先变成可测的距离，再变成公众关注的一份，最后变成谁都躲不开的显而易见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ridges fading into haze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道道山脊没入雾中。

branches.en: The weather branch: fifty metres on the motorway.
branches.cn: 天气分支：高速路上五十米。

branches.en: The sightline branch: trees blocking the path from the house.
branches.cn: 视线分支：树挡住从屋里看小路的视线。

branches.en: The attention branch: a small charity on national news.
branches.cn: 关注分支：小慈善机构上了全国新闻。

branches.en: The design branch: small text made readable by contrast.
branches.cn: 设计分支：靠对比度让小字可读。

branches.en: The plainness branch: a mistake everyone could see.
branches.cn: 明显分支：人人都看得见的错误。

intro.en: Vis- means to see, -ibilis and -ity make an adjective and then a quality, and in- negates it.
intro.cn: vis- 意为看见，-ibilis 与 -ity 依次造出形容词与性质名词，in- 表示否定。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visibilis are recorded, as is the medieval noun visibilitas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visibilis 均有记录，中世纪名词 visibilitas 同样有记录。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: The verb also gives vision and video.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还生出 vision 与 video。

definition_zh: 兴高采烈；提升；赞扬
definition_en: a feeling of great joy, or the act of raising someone in rank or praising them highly
core_image: 两双手把一个人高高举起，众人都要仰头看
scene: 毕业典礼上，她把帽子抛向空中，脸上全是压不住的狂喜。 A wave of exaltation swept over the graduates as the music began.
sceneCN: 这里 exaltation 是「兴高采烈、狂喜」（第 1 个义项：情绪被举高）；句意：音乐响起时，一阵狂喜掠过毕业生们。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「提升；颂扬；使兴奋」
动词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「地位高的；崇高的；兴奋的」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「令人振奋的；使人高尚的」

senses.title: A feeling of intense joy
senses.definition: a feeling of great joy and excitement that lifts the mind above its ordinary mood
senses.definitionCN: 极度喜悦与兴奋，心神被抬到日常情绪之上
senses.example: A sense of exaltation filled the hall as the choir rose.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团起立时，一种狂喜充满了大厅。
senses.why: Latin altus means high, so a lifted mind is the source image, and the noun names that upward surge of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altus 意为「高」，心神被举高正是这个词的画面来源，名词便指情绪向上涌起的状态。

senses.title: The act of raising to a high rank
senses.definition: the act of raising a person to a higher position, honour, or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 把人提升到更高职位、荣誉或地位的行为
senses.example: His exaltation to the chairmanship surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他被擢升为主席，谁也不感到意外。
senses.why: The verb exaltare means literally to lift up, so applied to persons the noun names the act of placing someone on higher ground.
senses.whyCN: 动词 exaltare 字面就是「举起来」，用在人身上，名词便指把人放到更高位置的这个动作。

senses.title: Praise or glorification
senses.definition: the act of praising someone or something highly, especially in worship
senses.definitionCN: 高度赞扬某人或某物，尤指在宗教崇拜中
senses.example: The psalm ends in the exaltation of the divine name.
senses.exampleCN: 这首圣诗以颂扬神名作结。
senses.why: To lift a name up in words is to praise it, so the same upward image moved from physical height into speech and worship.
senses.whyCN: 用言语把名字举高就是颂扬，同一个「向上」的意象于是从身体的高度转移到言说与崇拜里。

senses.title: A state of lofty dignity
senses.definition: the condition of being elevated in dignity, purity, or spiritual worth
senses.definitionCN: 在尊严、纯净或精神价值上处于高处的状态
senses.example: The old hymns speak of the exaltation of the soul after death.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的赞美诗谈到灵魂在死后得到的升华。
senses.why: Because height was read as worth, the noun also names a lasting elevated condition rather than a single act or a passing feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为「高」被读作「贵」，这个名词也指一种持久的高贵状态，而不只是一次举动或一阵情绪。

intro.en: Exaltation comes from Latin altus, high, through the verb exaltare, to lift up.
intro.cn: exaltation 源自拉丁语 altus（高），经由动词 exaltare（举高）而来。

items.en: Altus means high or lofty, and is generally taken as growing from alere, to nourish, in the sense of grown tall.
items.cn: altus 意为高的、崇高的，一般认为它源自 alere（养育），取「已经长高」之意。

items.en: The verb exaltare joins ex- to altus and means to lift up or to raise.
items.cn: 动词 exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成，意为举起、抬高。

items.en: The noun exaltatio names a lifting up, whether of a body, a rank, or a mood.
items.cn: 名词 exaltatio 指举起，可以是身体、地位或情绪上的举起。

items.en: Old French exaltation keeps both the religious and the social senses alive.
items.cn: 古法语 exaltation 同时让宗教与社会两方面的含义延续下来。

items.en: English adopts the word for raising in rank, for praise, and for lifted feeling.
items.cn: 英语采用这个词，用来表示提升地位、颂扬与情绪高涨。

items.en: In modern use the emotional sense of elation is the most common one.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，表示情绪高涨的「狂喜」义最为常见。

note.en: Exaltation belongs to the high family of altus, beside the verb exalt, and near the words for joy, raising, and praise.
note.cn: exaltation 属于 altus 的「高」词族，与动词 exalt 同根，并与表示喜悦、提升、赞扬的词相邻。

entries.definition: to raise in rank or to praise highly
high in rank, noble, or filled with joy
entries.definitionCN: 地位高的；崇高的；满心欢喜的

entries.definition: great rejoicing and triumph
entries.definitionCN: 欢腾与得意——与 exaltation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 exsultare「跳起」）

entries.definition: a mood of high spirits and joy
the act of raising something or the state of being raised
the act of praising something as glorious

normalIntro.en: Exaltation carries the Latin altus, high: something in the mind or in rank has been lifted.
normalIntro.cn: exaltation 带着拉丁语 altus（高）的底子：不是心神被举高，就是地位被举高。

normal.en: Exalt and exaltation share the Latin altus, which means high.
normal.cn: exalt 与 exaltation 共享拉丁语 altus，意为「高」。

normal.en: Altitude comes from the same altus, so height ties the whole family together.
normal.cn: altitude 也来自同一个 altus，高度把整个词族串在一起。

normal.en: Exultation looks alike but comes from exsultare, to leap up.
normal.cn: exultation 形似，却来自 exsultare（跳起来）。

normal.en: In worship, exaltation names the lifting of a name in praise.
normal.cn: 在崇拜中，exaltation 指把某个名字高举颂扬。

normal.en: Raise is the plain verb, while exalt is the literary and religious one.
normal.cn: raise 是平实的动词，exalt 则更文学、更宗教。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulled up by a gust until it rides above the rooftops.
abstract.cn: 想象风筝被一阵风拉起，一直升到屋顶之上。

abstract.en: See a hand lifting a young scholar onto a higher step of a stone stair.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把年轻学者托上石阶更高的一级。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd lift one name high above all the noise.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把一个名字高高举过所有喧哗。

examples.en: The crowd rose in a mood of pure exaltation.
examples.cn: 人群起身，沉浸在纯粹的狂喜之中。

examples.en: His exaltation to the rank of master came after thirty years of service.
examples.cn: 在服务三十年后，他被擢升为大师。

examples.en: The hymn is a song of exaltation, not of complaint.
examples.cn: 这首圣诗是一曲颂扬，而不是抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱个高台」——读起来像「爱个高台」，人往高台上一站，心就飘起来，既是被提升也是狂喜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）+ altus（高，一般认为源自 alere「养育、长高」）→ 动词 exaltare（举高、抬高）→ 名词 exaltatio → 英语 exaltation，核心义「把人或心举到高处」。

sensesIntro.en: Exaltation moves from a lifted feeling of joy, to the act of raising someone in rank, to praise, and finally to a lasting state of lofty dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: exaltation 从被举高的喜悦，走到把某人提升的举动，再到颂扬，最后指一种持久的高贵状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands lifting a person until the crowd must look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手把一个人举起，众人只能抬头看。

branches.en: Joy is the mind lifted above its usual level.
branches.cn: 喜悦就是心神被举到平常水平之上。

branches.en: Rank is the body placed on a higher step.
branches.cn: 地位就是把身体放上更高的一级台阶。

branches.en: Praise is a name lifted in speech and song.
branches.cn: 赞扬就是在言说与歌唱里把名字举高。

branches.en: Dignity is height that has become permanent.
branches.cn: 高贵是被固定下来的高度。

branches.en: Singing praise often produces the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 唱颂本身常常就会带来那种被举起的感觉。

intro.en: Exaltation combines the Latin prefix ex-, the root altus, high, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exaltation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 altus（高）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin altus means high or deep, and exaltare means to raise or to lift up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altus 意为高的、深的，exaltare 意为举高、抬高。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns height into a lifting.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把「高」变成了「举起」。
altus 描述高耸挺立之物。

items.example: Altus is generally taken to grow from alere.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 altus 源自 alere。
exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成。

items.example: Exaltatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exaltatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Exalt is the shorter English verb.
items.exampleCN: exalt 是更简短的英语动词。

items.example: Exultation comes from exsultare, to leap up.

definition_zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外；在战场上
definition_en: at a distance from home or from the usual place, especially in far afield; in older use, out in open country or on campaign
core_image: 离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去
scene: 这家小厂原本只卖给邻镇，如今客户远及海外。 The firm now sells far afield.
sceneCN: 这里 afield 是「在远处」（第 1 个义项：远离本地、到远方去）；句意为这家厂如今把货卖到很远的地方。核心画面是离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去。

pos.zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（副词，常与 far 或 further 连用）

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 a- 的名词，义为「田地；场地；领域」
field 加 work 构成，义为「实地考察；田野工作」
out 加 field 构成，义为「外场；外围地带」

senses.title: Far from home or the usual place
senses.definition: at a distance from the place where you live or normally work, especially in the phrase far afield
senses.definitionCN: 离你居住或平常工作的地方有一段距离，尤用于 far afield 这一短语
senses.example: Collectors come from far afield to see the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏爱好者从很远的地方赶来看这批藏品。
senses.why: The prefix a- here means on or in, so afield is literally in the field: once you leave your own plot you are out in open country, which is far from home.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 表示「在……上／中」，所以 afield 字面是「在田地里」：一旦离开自家那块地，你就到了外面的旷野，也就是离家很远的地方。

senses.title: Out on open ground or on campaign
senses.definition: out in the open country, or away on a military campaign, the older literal sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 在外面的旷野中，或出征在外，是该词更古老、更字面的用法
senses.example: The regiment spent a whole summer afield.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团整个夏天都在野外驻扎。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original picture unchanged: soldiers and hunters were literally in the fields, away from the town walls.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项原封不动地保留了最初的画面：士兵与猎人确实身处田野，远离城墙之内。

intro.en: Afield is a phrase worn down into one word: the Old English preposition on plus field, meaning in the field, later fused and extended to mean far from home.
intro.cn: afield 是一个短语磨损成的单词：古英语介词 on 加 field，意为「在田地里」，后来融合并引申为「远离家乡」。

items.en: Old English on meant on or in, and in casual speech it wore down to a single unstressed a-.
items.cn: 古英语 on 意为「在……上／中」，在口语中弱化为一个不重读的 a-。

items.en: Old English feld meant open country or unenclosed land, the ancestor of modern field.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为旷野或未围起的土地，是现代 field 的祖先。

items.en: The phrase on felde meant out in the open, used of grazing animals and of soldiers on campaign.
items.cn: 短语 on felde 意为「在旷野中」，用于放牧的牲畜与出征的士兵。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the two words had fused into afeld, written as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，两个词已融合为 afeld，写成一个副词。

items.en: Modern spelling restored the ie of field, and the adverb settled into far afield and further afield, meaning at a distance.
items.cn: 现代拼写恢复了 field 中的 ie，该副词固定用于 far afield 与 further afield，表示「在远处」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the a- adverbs built from nouns; the near-meaning group lists other ways of saying far away.
note.cn: 形近组保留由名词构成的 a- 类副词；近义组列出其他表示「在远处」的说法。

normalIntro.en: Afield is a-, on, plus field, open land: on the field, and therefore away from home.
normalIntro.cn: afield 就是 a-「在……上」加 field「田野」：在田野上，因此也就是离开家。

normal.en: The a- is the worn-down Old English on, the same a- you see in ashore, abroad and asleep.
normal.cn: 这个 a- 是古英语 on 的弱化形式，与 ashore、abroad、asleep 中的 a- 相同。

normal.en: Afield almost always follows far or further, so learn the pair far afield as one chunk.
normal.cn: afield 几乎总跟在 far 或 further 后面，所以把 far afield 当作一个整块来记。

normal.en: It is an adverb, never an adjective: say travellers from far afield, not afield travellers.
normal.cn: 它是副词，绝不作形容词：说 travellers from far afield，不说 afield travellers。

normal.en: Field means open land, so afield keeps the picture of stepping outside your own fence.
normal.cn: field 意为旷野，所以 afield 保留「走出自家围栏」的画面。

normal.en: Do not confuse afield with the field: the first tells where someone is, the second names the ground.
normal.cn: 别把 afield 与 the field 混淆：前者说人在哪里，后者指那块地。

abstract.en: Picture your own small plot, then the wide open country beyond its fence.
abstract.cn: 想象自家那一小块地，再想象围栏外辽阔的旷野。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier leaving the town gate and sleeping under the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一个士兵走出城门，在天空下露宿。

abstract.en: Think of a letter that travelled three provinces to reach your desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封跨越三个省才到你桌上的信。

examples.en: The magazine draws its writers from far afield.
examples.cn: 这份杂志的作者来自很远的地方。

examples.en: We had to look further afield for a supplier.
examples.cn: 我们不得不去更远的地方找供应商。

examples.en: Students who study afield often return with new ideas.
examples.cn: 到外地求学的学生回来时常带着新想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲尔德」——阿（a）菲（fi）尔（el）德（d）：走出家门那片田野（field），就是到远处、在野外。

root: 古英语介词 on「在……上」加 feld「旷野、未围之地」构成短语 on felde「在田野中」，十四世纪融合为 afeld，现代拼写恢复 field 的 ie，成为副词 afield，并固定用于 far 或 further afield 表示「在远处」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses start from one step outside the fence: the literal one puts you in open country or on campaign, and the extended one simply measures how far that step took you from home.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都从「走出围栏的那一步」出发：字面义把你放在旷野或出征途中，引申义只是衡量这一步把你带得离家有多远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: out of your own field, into the open
core.cn: 核心意象：离开自家那块地，走到外面的旷野

branches.en: Customers arriving from other provinces.
branches.cn: 客户从外省赶来。

branches.en: Searching beyond the usual local sources.
branches.cn: 到平常的本地渠道之外去寻找。

branches.en: Troops camping on open ground.
branches.cn: 部队在旷野扎营。

branches.en: Hunters working the fields all season.
branches.cn: 猎人整个季节都在田野里。

branches.en: Both put the subject outside the home fence.
branches.cn: 两者都把主体放在自家围栏之外。

intro.en: Afield belongs to a small English pattern where the preposition on wears down to a- and turns a noun into an adverb of place or state.
intro.cn: afield 属于英语中一个小构词模式：介词 on 弱化为 a-，把名词变成表示地点或状态的副词。

senses.title: The nut of the almond tree
senses.definition: the edible seed of the almond tree, oval and pointed at both ends, eaten as a nut or ground into flour
senses.definitionCN: 扁桃树的可食种子，椭圆形、两端尖，作坚果食用或磨成粉
senses.example: She scattered toasted almonds over the salad.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤过的杏仁撒在沙拉上。
senses.why: The word came from Greek amygdale, almond, through Latin and French, and the l was reinserted by scholars who knew the Latin spelling.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」，经拉丁语与法语传入，其中的 l 是懂拉丁拼写的学者重新加回去的。

senses.title: A pale warm brown colour
senses.definition: a pale, slightly warm brown colour like the skin of the nut, used in design and cosmetics
senses.definitionCN: 像杏仁外皮那样浅而略暖的褐色，用于设计与化妆品
senses.example: The walls were painted a soft almond.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面漆成了柔和的杏仁色。
senses.why: Here the nut lends its skin colour to the word, the same transfer that gives us chocolate, olive and salmon.
senses.whyCN: 这里坚果把它外皮的颜色借给了这个词，与 chocolate、olive、salmon 的转移方式相同。

intro.en: Almond travelled from Greek amygdale through Latin amygdala and Old French almande; the l in the modern spelling is a scholarly restoration.
intro.cn: almond 从希腊语 amygdale 经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 一路走来；现代拼写中的 l 是学者恢复的。

items.en: Greek amygdale meant almond, and it also named anything shaped like one, including a part of the brain.
items.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 意为杏仁，也指任何杏仁形状的东西，包括大脑的一个部分。

items.en: Latin amygdala kept both the nut and the shape sense, and gave English the anatomical term amygdala.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amygdala 保留坚果与形状两义，并为英语提供解剖学术语 amygdala。

items.en: Old French almande lost the g and the y, and the word entered Middle English as almande or almaunde.
items.cn: 古法语 almande 丢掉了 g 与 y，该词以 almande 或 almaunde 的形式进入中古英语。

items.en: Scribes who knew Latin put the l back, and by the fifteenth century almond was the usual spelling.
items.cn: 懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加了回去，到十五世纪 almond 成为常见拼写。

items.en: Modern almond names the nut, the tree, its milk and flour, and a pale brown colour used in design.
items.cn: 现代 almond 指坚果、树、它的奶与粉，以及设计中用到的一种浅褐色。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar shape; the near-meaning group lists other nuts and a neighbouring colour.
note.cn: 形近组保留形状相近的词；近义组列出其他坚果与相邻的颜色。

Money given to the poor.
To change something for the better.

entries.definition: A small round brown nut.

normalIntro.en: Almond comes from Greek amygdale, and the brain amygdala is named after the same nut shape.
normalIntro.cn: almond 来自希腊语 amygdale，大脑的 amygdala（杏仁核）正是按同一种坚果形状命名的。

normal.en: Almond and amygdala share one Greek root, so the brain region is literally almond-shaped.
normal.cn: almond 与 amygdala 共享一个希腊词根，所以那个脑区字面就是「杏仁形的」。

normal.en: The l is written but not pronounced: say AH-mund, not AL-mond.
normal.cn: l 写出来但不发音：读作 AH-mund，不是 AL-mond。

normal.en: Almond flour is ground nuts; almond milk is soaked and blended nuts.
normal.cn: almond flour 是磨碎的坚果，almond milk 是浸泡后打碎的坚果。

normal.en: It is countable as a nut, so say six almonds, but uncountable as a colour.
normal.cn: 指坚果时可数，所以说 six almonds；指颜色时不可数。

normal.en: Botanically the almond is a seed, not a true nut, but the kitchen calls it a nut.
normal.cn: 植物学上杏仁是种子，不是真正的坚果，但厨房里叫它坚果。

abstract.en: Picture a pointed brown seed inside a woody shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗两头尖的褐色种子藏在木质硬壳里。

abstract.en: Imagine an orchard of small trees with pale pink blossom.
abstract.cn: 想象一片小树林，开着淡粉色的花。

abstract.en: Think of a colour card the shade of the nut skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张色卡，正是坚果外皮的那个色度。

examples.en: The recipe calls for ground almonds and no wheat flour.
examples.cn: 这个配方要用杏仁粉，不用小麦面粉。

examples.en: Almond trees blossom early in the valley.
examples.cn: 山谷里的扁桃树开花很早。

examples.en: She chose almond for the bedroom walls.
examples.cn: 她为卧室墙面选了杏仁色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿蒙德」——阿（al）蒙（mon）德（d）：硬壳里蒙着一颗尖头种子，就是杏仁。

root: 希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 进入中古英语，懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加回拼写，形成 almond；同一词根还产生解剖学词 amygdala「杏仁核」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from one seed: the first names the nut you eat, and the second borrows the pale brown of its skin as a colour name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自同一颗种子：第一个指你吃的坚果，第二个借它外皮的浅褐色作为颜色名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointed brown seed in a hard shell
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳里一颗两头尖的褐色种子

branches.en: A handful of toasted nuts.
branches.cn: 一把烤过的坚果。

branches.en: Flour ground from blanched kernels.
branches.cn: 用去皮仁磨成的粉。

branches.en: A pale warm wall colour.
branches.cn: 浅而暖的墙面色。

branches.en: A lipstick shade named after the skin.
branches.cn: 以外皮命名的唇膏色号。

branches.en: Both start from the same seed.
branches.cn: 两者都从同一颗种子出发。

intro.en: Almond has no productive English affixes, but its Greek root amygdal- still builds scientific words, and -ine forms the cooking adjective.
intro.cn: almond 没有能产的英语词缀，但它的希腊词根 amygdal- 仍在造科学词，-ine 则构成烹饪形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek amygdale passed into Latin amygdala and then into Old French almande, where the g and y were lost.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 进入拉丁语成为 amygdala，再进入古法语成为 almande，途中丢掉了 g 与 y。

definition_zh: n. 氨；氨气；氨水（家用清洁剂）
definition_en: A colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a sharp smell, used in fertilisers and industry; its water solution is also called ammonia and used as a cleaner.
core_image: 一开盖就冲鼻子的那股刺鼻气味
scene: 她戴上手套才敢擦那面油腻的灶台。 The cleaner contains ammonia, so open a window first.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里的 ammonia 指含氨的清洁液，气味刺鼻，所以要先开窗通风。

derivatives.zh: 铵
氨的；含氨的
胺

senses.title: The gas and industrial chemical
senses.definition: a colourless gas of nitrogen and hydrogen with a sharp smell, made in bulk for fertilisers and refrigeration
senses.definitionCN: 由氮与氢构成、气味刺鼻的无色气体，大规模生产用于化肥与制冷
senses.example: The plant produces ammonia for fertiliser factories.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂为化肥厂生产氨。
senses.why: The name comes from sal ammoniac, a salt scraped near a desert shrine, so the word carries a place name into modern industry.
senses.whyCN: 名称来自 sal ammoniac「阿蒙神之盐」，那是在沙漠神殿附近刮取的盐，因此这个词把一个地名带进了现代工业。

senses.title: The household cleaner
senses.definition: a water solution of that gas, sold for cutting grease on glass and hard surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 该气体的水溶液，作为清除玻璃与硬表面油污的清洁剂出售
senses.example: Never mix ammonia with bleach in the same bucket.
senses.exampleCN: 绝不要把氨水与漂白剂混在同一只桶里。
senses.why: The same substance is meant, but the household sense names the bottle on the shelf rather than the molecule in the plant.
senses.whyCN: 指的是同一种物质，但家用义命指的是架子上的那瓶液体，而不是工厂里的分子。

intro.en: Ammonia is shortened from sal ammoniac, the salt of Ammon, collected near the desert shrine of the god Amun. Chemists kept the place name when they isolated the gas.
intro.cn: ammonia 由 sal ammoniac「阿蒙神之盐」缩略而来，那种盐是在阿蒙神的沙漠神殿附近采集的。化学家分离出这种气体时保留了那个地名。

items.en: The name Ammon comes from Greek Ammon, the Egyptian god Amun, whose desert shrine in Libya stood near deposits of a peculiar salt.
items.cn: Ammon 这个名字来自希腊语 Ammon，即埃及神阿蒙；他在利比亚的沙漠神殿附近有一种特殊盐的沉积。

items.en: Latin sal ammoniacus meant salt of Ammon, a crusty salt gathered from the ground near that shrine and used in medicine and metalwork.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sal ammoniacus 意为「阿蒙神之盐」，是在那座神殿附近地面采集的结壳盐，用于医药与金属加工。

items.en: Eighteenth-century chemists shortened sal ammoniac to ammonia once the gas had been isolated from that salt and recognised as a distinct substance.
items.cn: 18 世纪的化学家在从那种盐中分离出气体、并确认它是独立物质后，把 sal ammoniac 缩略为 ammonia。

items.en: English took ammonia in the late eighteenth century, first for the gas and soon for the watery solution sold as a household cleaner.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪后期借入 ammonia，先指气体，很快也指作为家用清洁剂出售的水溶液。

items.en: Ammonia now names a bulk industrial chemical, and the same base gives ammonium for the ion and amine for the wider family of compounds.
items.cn: ammonia 如今指一种大宗工业化学品，同一底座还产生表示离子的 ammonium 与表示更大家族化合物的 amine。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ammon- family and one similar opening; the near-meaning group lists other harsh cleaning chemicals.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ammon- 词族与一个相近开头；近义组列出其他刺激性清洁化学品。

entries.definition: The positive ion formed from ammonia.
A compound derived from ammonia.
entries.definitionCN: 由氨衍生的一类化合物。

entries.definition: Containing or like ammonia.
Loss of memory.

entries.definitionCN: 用于清洁的强碱性溶液。

entries.definition: A chemical that removes colour and stains.
entries.definitionCN: 去除颜色与污渍的化学品。

entries.definition: A substance that burns organic tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 能烧伤有机组织的物质。

entries.definition: A liquid that dissolves other substances.
entries.definitionCN: 能溶解其他物质的液体。

normalIntro.en: Ammonia is the salt of Ammon shortened, so link the sharp smell to a desert shrine.
normalIntro.cn: ammonia 是「阿蒙神之盐」的缩略，所以把那股刺鼻气味与一座沙漠神殿联系起来。

normal.en: Ammonia is the gas and the bottle; ammonium is the ion.
normal.cn: ammonia 是气体也是那瓶液体，ammonium 是离子。

normal.en: It is uncountable: some ammonia, not an ammonia.
normal.cn: 它不可数：some ammonia，不说 an ammonia。

normal.en: Never mix ammonia with bleach; the fumes are dangerous.
normal.cn: 绝不要把氨水与漂白剂混合，产生的气体有毒。

normal.en: The smell is sharp and stinging, not sweet.
normal.cn: 气味刺鼻蛰人，不是甜的。

normal.en: Do not confuse ammonia with amnesia, loss of memory.
normal.cn: 别把 ammonia 与 amnesia「记忆丧失」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a bottle that makes your eyes water before you touch it.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶还没碰到就让你眼睛发酸的液体。

abstract.en: Imagine a white crust scraped from desert ground.
abstract.cn: 想象从沙漠地面刮下的一层白壳。

abstract.en: Think of a fertiliser plant breathing out a sharp cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一家化肥厂呼出一团刺鼻的雾。

examples.en: Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen under pressure.
examples.cn: 氨由氮与氢在加压条件下合成。

examples.en: The ammonia smell told us the tank was leaking.
examples.cn: 那股氨味告诉我们储罐在泄漏。

examples.en: She diluted the ammonia before wiping the glass.
examples.cn: 她把氨水稀释后再擦玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿摩尼亚」——阿摩（ammo）尼亚（nia）：一摩（摸）就「你呀」地叫起来，那股冲鼻子的味道就是氨。

root: 埃及神阿蒙之名经希腊语 Ammon 进入拉丁语 sal ammoniacus「阿蒙神之盐」，18 世纪化学家缩略为 ammonia 指从该盐分离出的气体，再引申指家用氨水。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one substance in two places: the molecule made in a plant, and the bottle kept under a sink.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种物质的两个所在：工厂里造出的分子，以及水槽下放着的那瓶液体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp smell that rushes at your nose
core.cn: 核心意象：一开盖就冲鼻子的那股刺鼻气味

branches.en: A plant making fertiliser feedstock.
branches.cn: 一家生产化肥原料的工厂。

branches.en: A leaking tank in a cold store.
branches.cn: 冷库里泄漏的储罐。

branches.en: A bottle under the kitchen sink.
branches.cn: 厨房水槽下的一瓶清洁剂。

branches.en: A window opened before wiping grease.
branches.cn: 擦油污前先打开的窗。

branches.en: One molecule, industrial then domestic.
branches.cn: 同一种分子，先工业用，再家用。

intro.en: Ammonia keeps the name root ammon- plus the substance ending -ia, and shifts to -ium for the ion.
intro.cn: ammonia 保留名称词根 ammon- 加物质词尾 -ia，变成离子时改用 -ium。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sal ammoniacus, salt of Ammon; New Latin cut it to ammonia, and chemistry added ammonium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 sal ammoniacus「阿蒙神之盐」；新拉丁语把它缩略为 ammonia，化学又加上 ammonium。

latinEntries.example: Sal ammoniacus is the old name.
New Latin cut the phrase short.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 新拉丁语把该短语缩略。

definition_zh: 建造；竖立；竖直的
definition_en: to build something or raise it upright, or standing straight up

scene: 工人们在广场上竖起了一座纪念碑。 Workers erected a monument in the square.

senses.title: To build or set up
senses.definition: to build a structure or set something upright in place
senses.definitionCN: 建造建筑物或把某物立起来安置好
senses.example: They erected a bridge across the narrow river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在狭窄的河上建了一座桥。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to raise up, so building and setting upright share one core action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向上竖起，因此建造与竖立共享同一个核心动作。

senses.title: To raise into an upright position
senses.definition: to lift or straighten something so that it stands vertically
senses.definitionCN: 把某物抬起或扶正，使其垂直立起
senses.example: The campers erected their tent before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 露营者在天黑前搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: The physical act of raising is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 向上抬起的身体动作，是这个词最古老的含义层。

senses.title: Standing straight up
senses.definition: standing or pointing straight upward, used as an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 笔直站立或指向上方，作形容词使用
senses.example: He sat with an erect back throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中他都挺直着背坐着。
senses.why: The past participle became an adjective describing the upright result.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词转化为形容词，描述竖立后的状态。

intro.en: Erect comes from Latin erigere, to raise up, from e-, out, and regere, to guide or keep straight.
intro.cn: erect 来自拉丁语 erigere（向上竖起），由 e-（向外）与 regere（引导、使直）构成。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使直。

items.cn: 这里的 e- 表示向外或向上。

definition_zh: 偿付能力（资产足以覆盖负债、能按期清偿债务的能力）
definition_en: the ability to meet long-term debts because assets exceed liabilities

senses.title: The ability to pay long-term debts
senses.definition: the condition of being able to meet debts as they fall due out of one's own resources
senses.definitionCN: 能以自己的资源在债务到期时予以清偿的状态
senses.example: The auditors questioned the firm's solvency after two loss-making years.
senses.exampleCN: 连续两年亏损之后，审计师质疑该企业的偿付能力。
senses.why: the noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to loosen or to pay, so solvency is literally the state of being able to untie what one owes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自拉丁语中「松开、清偿」的动词，因此偿付能力字面上就是「能够解开所欠之债」的状态。

senses.title: The balance-sheet test of assets over liabilities
senses.titleCN: 资产负债表上的资产大于负债
senses.definition: the arithmetic condition in which total assets exceed total liabilities
senses.definitionCN: 总资产超过总负债的算术条件
senses.example: On paper the company passed the solvency test with room to spare.
senses.exampleCN: 账面上，这家公司通过偿付检验，还有余量。
senses.why: once debts are written down as liabilities, being able to pay becomes a comparison of two totals rather than a promise.
senses.whyCN: 债务一旦记为负债，能否清偿就变成两个总额的比较，而不是一句承诺。

senses.title: Regulatory solvency for banks
senses.titleCN: 银行监管意义上的偿付能力
senses.definition: the capital a bank must hold above its risk-weighted assets to absorb losses
senses.definitionCN: 银行必须在风险加权资产之上持有、用于吸收损失的资本
senses.example: The bank was told to raise capital to restore its solvency ratio.
senses.exampleCN: 该行被要求补充资本，以恢复偿付能力比率。
senses.why: a bank's losses can exceed its capital in a single quarter, so a regulator demands a buffer before that happens.
senses.whyCN: 银行一个季度的损失就可能超过资本，监管者因此要求事前留出缓冲。

senses.title: Solvency capital for insurers
senses.titleCN: 保险公司的偿付能力资本
senses.definition: the funds an insurer must keep so that it can pay claims even after a large shock
senses.definitionCN: 保险公司即使遭遇重大冲击后仍能赔付所需的资金
senses.example: The insurer held solvency capital well above the minimum.
senses.exampleCN: 这家保险公司持有的偿付能力资本远高于最低要求。
senses.why: claims arrive after a shock, so an insurer must hold funds that can be paid out even in a bad year.
senses.whyCN: 赔付在冲击之后才到来，保险公司必须持有即使坏年份也能付出的资金。

senses.title: A corporate solvency crisis
senses.definition: a situation in which a firm's assets no longer cover its debts and rescue becomes urgent
senses.definitionCN: 企业资产已不足以覆盖债务、亟需救助的局面
senses.example: The solvency crisis began when the pension deficit was counted.
senses.exampleCN: 偿付能力危机在养老金缺口被计入时开始。
senses.why: a pension deficit can turn a profitable firm into one whose assets no longer cover its promises.
senses.whyCN: 养老金缺口能把一家盈利企业变成资产不再覆盖承诺的企业。

senses.title: Sovereign solvency
senses.definition: the ability of a state to service its public debt without default
senses.definitionCN: 一国在不违约的情况下偿还公共债务的能力
senses.example: Sovereign solvency depends on growth as much as on the deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 国家的偿付能力既取决于赤字，也同样取决于增长。
senses.why: a state cannot be liquidated, so its solvency is judged by its capacity to tax and grow rather than by a sale.
senses.whyCN: 国家不能被变卖，其偿付能力因此以征税与增长能力而非出售来评判。

senses.title: The solvency ratio as a number
senses.titleCN: 作为数字的偿付能力比率
senses.definition: a measure comparing capital or assets with liabilities or risk exposures
senses.definitionCN: 比较资本或资产与负债或风险敞口的指标
senses.example: A solvency ratio of one means assets exactly equal liabilities.
senses.exampleCN: 偿付能力比率等于一，意味着资产恰好等于负债。
senses.why: a single number lets supervisors compare very different institutions, so the condition is compressed into a ratio.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字能让监管者比较差别很大的机构，状态因此被压成比率。

senses.title: Solvency of a pension fund
senses.definition: whether a fund's assets plus expected income can cover the promises it has made
senses.definitionCN: 基金的资产加上预期收入能否覆盖其已作出的承诺
senses.example: The fund's solvency improved as bond yields rose.
senses.exampleCN: 随着债券收益率上升，该基金的偿付能力有所改善。
senses.why: promises extend decades beyond the assets on hand, so the fund must be judged against future payments.
senses.whyCN: 承诺比手头资产延伸得多数十年，基金因此必须对着未来支付来评判。

intro.en: Solvency comes from Latin solvere 'to loosen, to pay' through the present participle solvens and Late Latin solventia. English formed the noun in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solvency 经拉丁 solvere「松开、清偿」的现在分词 solvens 与晚期拉丁 solventia 而来，英语在 18 世纪构成该名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, and also to pay'. The paying sense grew from the image of untying a debt, and the deeper origin is usually analysed as a prefix plus a verb for loosening, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解」，也指「清偿」。清偿义从「解开债务」的意象生长出来；更深来源通常分析为前缀加「松开」动词，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The present participle solvens 'loosening, paying' described a person or estate that could meet its obligations.
items.cn: 现在分词 solvens「正在松开、正在清偿」描述能够履行义务的人或产业。

items.en: Late Latin solventia named the capacity to pay, and the abstract noun passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 solventia 指清偿能力，这一抽象名词经法语进入英语。

items.en: English solvency is recorded in commercial writing of the early eighteenth century, in contrast with insolvency.
items.cn: 英语 solvency 见于 18 世纪初的商业写作，与无力偿付相对。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries turned the idea into ratios, as banks and insurers were required to hold capital against losses.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪把这一观念变成比率，银行与保险公司被要求持有资本以抵御损失。

items.en: Pension funds, sovereigns and whole financial systems are now tested for solvency, so the word covers every scale of debtor.
items.cn: 养老基金、国家乃至整个金融体系如今都要接受偿付能力检验，这个词因此覆盖各种规模的债务人。

note.en: Group one holds words from the loosening root; group two holds terms that measure a different kind of financial health.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「松开」词根的词；第二组是衡量另一种财务健康的术语。

entries.tag: the adjective also a chemical noun
entries.definition: Able to pay debts; the same form also names a dissolving liquid, so context decides.
entries.definitionCN: 指有能力偿债；同一形式也指溶解液体，须靠语境分辨。

entries.definition: The inability to pay debts; it is the state that bankruptcy procedures address.
entries.definitionCN: 指无力偿债；正是破产程序所处理的状态。

entries.definition: An answer to a problem, or a liquid mixture; both come from loosening, not from paying.
entries.definitionCN: 指问题的解答或液体混合物；二者都出自「松开」而非「清偿」。

entries.definition: To break a substance into a liquid, or to end an assembly; the paying sense is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 指使物质溶入液体或解散集会；不含清偿义。

entries.definition: Whether cash is available this week; solvency asks whether assets cover debts at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指这周是否有现金可用；偿付能力问资产是否根本覆盖债务。

entries.definition: How safe a borrower looks to a lender; it is a judgement, while solvency is an accounting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指借款人在放贷者眼中的安全程度；它是判断，而偿付能力是会计条件。

entries.definition: The ratio of capital to risk-weighted assets; it is the banking test of solvency in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指资本与风险加权资产的比率；它是偿付能力在银行实践中的检验。

entries.definition: Failure to pay on time; a single default may be cured, while insolvency is a lasting condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指未能按时付款；单次违约可以补救，而无力偿债是持续状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: To solve and to pay are the same verb in Latin: untying a debt and untying a knot share an image.
normal.cn: 在拉丁语里，「解决」与「清偿」是同一个动词：解开债务与解开绳结共用同一意象。

normal.en: The family runs solve, solution, solvent, solvency, insolvent, insolvency, dissolve.
normal.cn: 同族词包括解决、解法、溶剂、偿付能力、无力偿付的、无力偿付、溶解。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the tests: solvency ratio, solvency risk, solvency capital requirement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出检验：偿付能力比率、偿付能力风险、偿付能力资本要求。

normal.en: Solvency compares totals on a balance sheet; liquidity compares cash with this month's bills.
normal.cn: 偿付能力比较资产负债表上的总额；流动性比较现金与本月的账单。

normal.en: The opposite is not bankruptcy but insolvency: the condition comes first, the procedure later.
normal.cn: 反义不是破产而是无力偿付：状态先出现，程序随后才来。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with assets on one pan and debts on the other, still tipped toward the assets.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一盘资产、一盘债务，仍向资产一端倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a knot being untied slowly, one debt at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结被慢慢解开，一次一笔债务。

abstract.en: Picture a hospital chart where the vital sign is not pulse but the gap between two totals.
abstract.cn: 想象一张病房图表，关键指标不是脉搏，而是两个总额之间的差。

examples.en: Solvency is a question of totals, not of this month's cash.
examples.cn: 偿付能力是总额的问题，而不是本月现金的问题。

examples.en: The regulator closed the bank once its solvency ratio fell below the floor.
examples.cn: 偿付能力比率跌破下限后，监管者关闭了这家银行。

examples.en: Rising rates improved the pension fund's solvency without any new contributions.
examples.cn: 利率上升改善了养老基金的偿付能力，且无需任何新缴款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解开」的词根加名词后缀——能把欠下的债一个个解开，就是有偿付能力

root: 拉丁 solvere「松开、解开、清偿」= 前缀「分开」+ 表示「松开」的动词，更深来源属重构；其现在分词 solvens 与晚期拉丁 solventia 给出 solvency，18 世纪入英语。同根词有 solve、solution、dissolve、dissolution。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all weigh two totals: what is owned against what is owed. The weighing is done for a firm, a balance sheet, a bank, an insurer, a failing company, a state, a published ratio and a pension fund.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在称量两个总额：拥有的与欠下的。称量对象分别是企业、资产负债表、银行、保险公司、陷入困境的公司、国家、公开的比率与养老基金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with assets on one pan and debts on the other, still tipped toward assets.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一盘资产、一盘债务，仍向资产一端倾斜。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY AND THE SUM: being able to pay, and the arithmetic that shows it.
branches.cn: 能力与总和：能够清偿，以及证明这一点的算术。

branches.en: REGULATED CAPITAL: banks and insurers must hold a buffer above expected losses.
branches.cn: 受监管的资本：银行与保险公司必须在预期损失之上持有缓冲。

branches.en: THE FIRM IN TROUBLE: when assets no longer cover debts, rescue becomes urgent.
branches.cn: 陷入困境的企业：资产不再覆盖债务时，救助变得急迫。

branches.en: THE STATE AS DEBTOR: a country's growth and deficit decide whether it can service its debt.
branches.cn: 作为债务人的国家：增长与赤字决定它能否偿还债务。

branches.en: NUMBERS AND PROMISES: a ratio is published, and a fund is tested against promises made long ago.
branches.cn: 数字与承诺：比率被公布，基金则要对着多年前作出的承诺受检。

intro.en: Solvency is an abstract noun built on a Latin verb for loosening, which also supplies the words for solving and dissolving.
intro.cn: solvency 是建立在拉丁语「松开」动词上的抽象名词，同一动词还给出「解决」与「溶解」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere and its participle solvens stand behind solve, solution, solvent, solvency and dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 及其分词 solvens 支撑 solve、solution、solvent、solvency 与 dissolve。

items.example: The verb joins a knot and a debt.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时连接绳结与债务。

items.meaning: an untying; an answer; a liquid mixture

items.exampleCN: 这家企业仍有偿付能力。

items.meaning: the state of being unable to pay

items.example: The dissolution of the partnership took a year.
items.exampleCN: 合伙关系的解散花了一年。

definition_zh: n. 飞行员；飞机驾驶员（语体偏旧或正式）；复数亦指飞行员式太阳镜
definition_en: A person who flies an aircraft, a slightly old-fashioned or formal word for a pilot; in the plural, a style of sunglasses.
core_image: 戴风镜坐在敞开座舱里的那个人
