sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aviator 指驾驶飞机的人，语体偏旧，常见于早期飞行与军事语境。

derivatives.zh: 航空；航空业
驾驶飞机
女飞行员
鸟舍；大型鸟笼

senses.title: A person who flies
senses.definition: someone who pilots an aircraft, especially in early or military contexts
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶航空器的人，尤用于早期飞行或军事语境
senses.example: The aviator logged nine hundred hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那位飞行员记录了九百小时飞行。
senses.why: Aviator adds the doer ending -or to the bird root avi, so it names the person who does the bird craft.
senses.whyCN: aviator 在「鸟」词根 avi 上加施事后缀 -or，因此指从事仿鸟之技的那个人。

senses.title: A style named after them
senses.definition: in the plural, a style of sunglasses with large teardrop lenses, from the eyewear of early pilots
senses.definitionCN: 用复数时指一种大水滴形镜片的太阳镜样式，源自早期飞行员的护目镜
senses.example: He wore aviators against the glare.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着飞行员式太阳镜挡强光。
senses.why: The kit of early flyers became a fashion, so the plural of the job title turned into the name of the glasses.
senses.whyCN: 早期飞行员的装备变成了时尚，于是这个职业名称的复数形式成了那种眼镜的名字。

intro.en: Aviator comes from Latin avis, bird, through French aviateur, formed in the 1860s alongside aviation and taken into English soon after.
intro.cn: aviator 出自拉丁语 avis「鸟」，经法语 aviateur 而来；该词于 1860 年代与 aviation 一同造出，随后不久进入英语。

items.en: A root meaning bird also gave the Latin avis and the English word aviary.
items.cn: 一个表示「鸟」的词根同时产生拉丁语 avis 与英语 aviary。

items.en: Latin avis meant bird, the model chosen when flight was still a dream.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为「鸟」，是飞行仍属梦想时选定的范本。

items.en: French formed aviateur from avis on the pattern of navigateur, a navigator.
items.cn: 法语按 navigateur「航行者」的样式，由 avis 造出 aviateur。

items.en: English adopted aviator before anyone had flown a powered machine.
items.cn: 英语在动力飞行出现之前就借入了 aviator。

items.en: Two world wars made aviator the standard formal title in the armed services.
items.cn: 两次世界大战使 aviator 成为军队中的标准正式称谓。

items.en: In the twentieth century the plural named the teardrop sunglasses of military pilots.
items.cn: 二十世纪其复数形式用来指军用飞行员的水滴形太阳镜。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the avi family and one other doer noun; the near-meaning group lists everyday and service words for a flyer.
note.cn: 形近组保留 avi 词族和另一个施事名词；近义组列出表示飞行者的日常与军种用词。

A woman who flies aircraft.
A large enclosure for birds.
One who plots a course.
The everyday word for a flyer.

A person who flies.
The people who work in flight.

normalIntro.en: Aviator is avi, bird, plus -or, the doer: the person who does what birds do.
normalIntro.cn: aviator 是 avi「鸟」加 -or「做……的人」：做鸟所做之事的那个人。

normal.en: Pilot is the everyday word; aviator is formal.
normal.cn: pilot 是日常用词，aviator 偏正式。

normal.en: Naval aviator is a set service title.
normal.cn: naval aviator 是固定军种称谓。

normal.en: The female form is aviatrix.
normal.cn: 女性形式是 aviatrix。

normal.en: Aviators also means a shape of sunglasses.
normal.cn: aviators 也指一种太阳镜样式。

normal.en: The field is aviation, the person is aviator.
normal.cn: 领域是 aviation，人是 aviator。

abstract.en: Picture goggles pushed up on a forehead.
abstract.cn: 想象风镜推到额头上。

abstract.en: Imagine an open cockpit and a scarf in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象敞开的座舱与风中的围巾。

abstract.en: Think of a logbook thick with hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记满小时数的飞行日志。

examples.en: The young aviator crossed the channel alone.
examples.cn: 那位年轻飞行员独自飞越海峡。

examples.en: Naval aviators train on carriers.
examples.cn: 海军飞行员在航母上训练。

examples.en: She bought a pair of aviators.
examples.cn: 她买了一副飞行员式太阳镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avi「鸟」+ -ator「做……的人」——像鸟一样飞的人，就是 aviator 飞行员。

root: 拉丁语 avis「鸟」在法语中按 navigateur 的样式造出 aviateur，英语 1866 年借作 aviator；两次世界大战后成为军中正式称谓，复数又指飞行员式太阳镜。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from the same kit: the person who flies like a bird, and the eyewear that person made famous.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项出自同一套装备：像鸟一样飞行的人，以及被这个人带火的那副眼镜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in goggles sitting in an open cockpit
core.cn: 核心意象：戴风镜坐在敞开座舱里的那个人

branches.en: A pilot beside a biplane.
branches.cn: 站在双翼机旁的飞行员。

branches.en: A logbook of nine hundred hours.
branches.cn: 记着九百小时的日志。

branches.en: Teardrop lenses against the glare.
branches.cn: 挡强光的水滴形镜片。

branches.en: A pair bought for style.
branches.cn: 为样式买的一副眼镜。

branches.en: The kit named after its wearer.
branches.cn: 以穿戴者命名的装备。

intro.en: Aviator is avi plus -ator; the same doer ending builds navigator and operator, while -trix marks the female form.
intro.cn: aviator 是 avi 加 -ator；同一施事后缀构成 navigator 与 operator，而 -trix 标记女性形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is avis, bird; the ending -ator is the Latin agent suffix, and Greek nautes gives navigator beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 avis「鸟」；词尾 -ator 是拉丁语施事后缀，旁边的希腊语 nautes 给出 navigator。

definition_zh: 机场；飞机场（尤指小型或军用）；简易起降场
definition_en: an area of level ground with runways where aircraft take off and land, usually smaller than a full airport and often military or temporary
core_image: 一片专门留给飞机起落的场地
scene: 小镇外那块草地战时停过运输机，如今只剩一条旧跑道。 The airfield closed to traffic in spring.
sceneCN: 这里 airfield 是「机场」（第 1 个义项：供飞机起降的场地，常指小型或军用）；句意为这座机场在春天停止通航。核心画面是一片专门留给飞机起落的场地。

pos.zh: 机场；飞机场（尤指小型或军用）

derivatives.zh: 同用 air- 的名词，义为「飞行器；飞机」
air 加 strip，义为「简易跑道；小型起降场」
去掉 air- 的部分，义为「场地；田野」

senses.title: Ground where aircraft take off and land
senses.definition: an area of level ground with runways where aircraft take off and land, usually smaller than a full airport and often military
senses.definitionCN: 带有跑道、供飞机起降的平整场地，通常比完整的航空港小，且常为军用
senses.example: The relief flight landed on a muddy airfield.
senses.exampleCN: 救援航班降落在一个泥泞的机场上。
senses.why: Air plus field is literally a field for the air: the word keeps the older sense of field as open ground set aside for one purpose.
senses.whyCN: air 加 field 字面就是「给空中用的场地」：该词保留了 field 的旧义，即为某一用途留出的开阔地面。

senses.title: A wartime or rural landing ground
senses.definition: a temporary or improvised strip used by military or small private aircraft, the sense most common in historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 军用或小型私人飞机使用的临时或简易起降地带，是历史类文本中最常见的用法
senses.example: They built an airfield in six weeks on farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在农田上六周就建成了一座简易机场。
senses.why: Here field keeps its farming meaning: an airfield of this kind really was a farm field with the crops cleared away.
senses.whyCN: 这里 field 保留了农事的含义：这类机场确实就是把庄稼清掉的一块农田。

intro.en: Airfield is a plain English compound: air, the sky, plus field, open ground, naming a field reserved for machines that fly.
intro.cn: airfield 是一个朴素的英语复合词：air「天空」加 field「开阔地面」，指留给飞行机器的一块场地。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or mist, and it is the ultimate source of the English noun air.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为空气或雾气，是英语名词 air 的最终来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer unchanged, and Old French air passed it into Middle English after the Norman conquest.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入 aer，诺曼征服后古法语 air 把它传入中古英语。

items.en: Old English feld meant open, unenclosed ground, the ancestor of modern field.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为开阔、未围起的土地，是现代 field 的祖先。

items.en: English joined air to field during the First World War, when flying grounds were literally marked-out fields.
items.cn: 英语在第一次世界大战期间把 air 与 field 拼合，当时的飞行场地确实就是划出来的田地。

items.en: Today airfield usually suggests a small or military site, while airport names the larger civil hub with terminals.
items.cn: 如今 airfield 多指小型或军用场地，而 airport 指带航站楼的较大民用枢纽。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the air- compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for a place where aircraft land.
note.cn: 形近组保留 air- 复合词；近义组列出其他表示「飞机起降场所」的词。

entries.definition: Any machine able to fly in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能在空中飞行的机器。

entries.definition: A narrow strip of ground used as a runway.
A company that carries passengers by air.
entries.definitionCN: 用飞机运送旅客的公司。

entries.definition: Far from home or the usual place.
entries.definitionCN: 远离家乡或平常所在之处。

entries.definition: A large site with runways and passenger terminals.
entries.definitionCN: 带跑道与旅客航站楼的大型场所。

entries.definition: A small airport, the older British term.
entries.definitionCN: 小型机场，是较旧的英式说法。

entries.definition: The paved strip aircraft use to take off.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机起飞所用的铺装长条地带。

entries.definition: A small landing area for helicopters.
entries.definitionCN: 供直升机起降的小块场地。

normalIntro.en: Airfield is air plus field: a field kept for the air, that is, for aircraft.
normalIntro.cn: airfield 就是 air 加 field：留给空中使用的场地，也就是留给飞机的场地。

normal.en: Field here means open ground, not a subject of study, so picture grass and a runway.
normal.cn: 这里的 field 指开阔地面，不是学科，所以想象草地和一条跑道。

normal.en: Airfield is smaller and simpler than airport: no terminal, just a strip.
normal.cn: airfield 比 airport 更小更简单：没有航站楼，只有一条跑道。

normal.en: Military writing prefers airfield; travel writing prefers airport.
normal.cn: 军事文本偏爱 airfield，旅行文本偏爱 airport。

normal.en: It is countable, so say two disused airfields, not two airfield.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 two disused airfields，不说 two airfield。

normal.en: Do not confuse airfield with afield: one is a place, the other tells how far away.
normal.cn: 别把 airfield 与 afield 混淆：一个是地点，另一个说距离有多远。

abstract.en: Picture a wheat field with the wheat rolled flat into a runway.
abstract.cn: 想象一片麦田，麦子被压平成一条跑道。

abstract.en: Imagine a village whose only landmark is a windsock on a pole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄，唯一的地标是杆子上的风向袋。

abstract.en: Think of a field that swapped its crop for aircraft.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田地，把庄稼换成了飞机。

examples.en: The old airfield is now a business park.
examples.cn: 那座旧机场如今是个商务园区。

examples.en: Fog closed the airfield for most of the morning.
examples.cn: 大雾让机场整个上午大部分时间无法使用。

examples.en: They taxied across the airfield to the hangar.
examples.cn: 他们滑行穿过机场来到机库。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「艾尔菲尔德」——艾尔（air）是天，菲尔德（field）是地：天上来的东西落在地上那块场子，就是机场。

root: air 源自希腊语 aer「空气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语；field 源自古英语 feld「开阔未围之地」。两者在第一次世界大战期间拼合为 airfield，字面即「留给飞行器的场地」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one patch of ground reserved for flying: the general sense covers any such site, and the narrower one recalls the improvised farm strips of wartime.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一块留给飞行的地面：通用义涵盖任何这类场地，较窄的用法则让人想起战时临时开辟的农田跑道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field reserved for the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一块留给天空的场地

branches.en: A runway laid on level ground.
branches.cn: 铺在平整地面上的一条跑道。

branches.en: A small site without terminals.
branches.cn: 没有航站楼的小型场地。

branches.en: Farmland cleared for wartime flights.
branches.cn: 为战时飞行清空的农田。

branches.en: A temporary strip that later disappears.
branches.cn: 一条后来又消失的临时跑道。

branches.en: Both keep field as open ground.
branches.cn: 两者都保留 field 的「开阔地面」义。

intro.en: Airfield belongs to the air- compound family, where air names the medium and the second noun names the thing built for it.
intro.cn: airfield 属于 air- 复合词族：air 指媒介，后一个名词指为它建造的东西。

latinIntro.en: Only the air half has a classical source, Greek aer through Latin aer; field is wholly Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 air 这一半有古典来源，即希腊语 aer 经拉丁语 aer；field 完全来自古英语。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the source of air.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是 air 的来源。

definition_zh: adj. 厌氧的；无氧的；（运动）无氧的
definition_en: Living or occurring without free oxygen; of exercise, short and intense enough that the muscles work without extra oxygen.
core_image: 把氧气抽走之后，生命仍在那儿硬撑
scene: 沼气池里的细菌不需要氧气也能分解秸秆。 Anaerobic bacteria break down the straw in the tank.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：沼气池是缺氧环境，里面分解秸秆的细菌属于厌氧菌，所以用 anaerobic 描述。

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

derivatives.zh: 需氧的；有氧的
厌氧生物
厌氧地；无氧地

senses.title: Life without oxygen
senses.definition: living, growing or occurring in the absence of free oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 在没有游离氧的环境中生存、生长或发生的
senses.example: Anaerobic digestion turns waste into methane.
senses.exampleCN: 厌氧消化把废弃物转化为甲烷。
senses.why: The prefix an- means without, aer is air and bios is life, so the word literally says life without air.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 an- 意为「没有」，aer 是空气，bios 是生命，所以这个词字面上说的就是「没有空气的生命」。

senses.title: Short hard exercise
senses.definition: of exercise so brief and intense that the muscles draw energy without waiting for oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 指运动短促而剧烈，肌肉不等氧气供应就取用能量
senses.example: Sprinting is anaerobic; a long jog is aerobic.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑是无氧运动，长时间慢跑是有氧运动。
senses.why: The same absence is meant, but now inside a muscle: the effort outruns the oxygen supply, so the body borrows another route.
senses.whyCN: 所指的仍是同一种「缺」，只是发生在肌肉内部：用力超过了供氧速度，身体便借用另一条路径。

intro.en: Anaerobic is Greek an-, without, plus aer, air, plus bios, life. Pasteur coined the French pair aerobie and anaerobie in the 1860s, and English took both.
intro.cn: anaerobic 由希腊语 an-「没有」加 aer「空气」加 bios「生命」构成。巴斯德在 19 世纪 60 年代造出法语的 aerobie 与 anaerobie 这一对，英语把两者都借入。

items.en: Greek an- is the form a- takes before a vowel, meaning not or without. It gives anaemia, anonymous and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 是 a- 在元音前的形式，意为「不、没有」。它产生 anaemia、anonymous 与 anarchy。

items.en: Greek aer meant air or mist, and gives aerial, aerate and aerodynamics.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气、雾气」，产生 aerial、aerate 与 aerodynamics。

items.en: Greek bios meant life, the same piece that builds biology and amphibian.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，与构成 biology 和 amphibian 的是同一个部件。

items.en: Pasteur coined French anaerobie in the 1860s for organisms that live without free oxygen, pairing it with aerobie.
items.cn: 巴斯德在 19 世纪 60 年代造出法语 anaerobie，指无需游离氧而生活的生物，与 aerobie 配对。

items.en: English took anaerobic from that pair, and sport science later borrowed it for effort that outruns the oxygen supply.
items.cn: 英语从这一对中借入 anaerobic，运动科学后来又把它借去指超过供氧速度的用力。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the aerobe family and two an- words; the near-meaning group lists other terms for low-oxygen conditions.
note.cn: 形近组保留 aerobe 词族与两个 an- 开头的词；近义组列出其他表示低氧状态的术语。

entries.definition: Requiring free oxygen.
An organism that lives without oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 无需氧气而生活的生物。

entries.definition: Loss of sensation induced for surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 为手术诱导的感觉丧失。

entries.definition: Building larger molecules in the body.
entries.definitionCN: 在体内合成较大分子的。

entries.definition: Containing no oxygen at all.
Having too little oxygen.
Describing conditions that strip oxygen away.

normalIntro.en: Anaerobic is an- plus aer plus bic: no air, so life that runs without oxygen.
normalIntro.cn: anaerobic 就是 an- 加 aer 加 bic：没有空气，所以是不靠氧气运行的生命。

normal.en: Drop the an- and you get aerobic, the exact opposite.
normal.cn: 去掉 an- 就得到 aerobic，正好相反。

normal.en: Anaerobic digestion makes methane; aerobic composting makes heat.
normal.cn: 厌氧消化产甲烷，好氧堆肥产热。

normal.en: Sprinting and lifting are anaerobic; jogging is aerobic.
normal.cn: 短跑与举重是无氧的，慢跑是有氧的。

normal.en: The noun for the organism is an anaerobe.
normal.cn: 指该生物的名词是 anaerobe。

normal.en: Do not confuse anaerobic with anabolic, which is about building tissue.
normal.cn: 别把 anaerobic 与 anabolic 混淆，后者讲合成组织。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed tank bubbling without any air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密闭罐子在毫无空气的情况下冒泡。

abstract.en: Imagine a sprinter finishing before the lungs catch up.
abstract.cn: 想象短跑者在肺还没跟上时就已冲线。

abstract.en: Think of mud at the bottom of a pond, black and airless.
abstract.cn: 想象池底的黑泥，没有一丝空气。

examples.en: Anaerobic bacteria thrive deep in the sediment.
examples.cn: 厌氧菌在沉积物深处繁盛。

examples.en: The treatment plant uses anaerobic digestion to cut sludge.
examples.cn: 处理厂用厌氧消化来减少污泥。

examples.en: Heavy lifting is largely anaerobic work.
examples.cn: 大重量举重主要是无氧做功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ aero「空气」+ bic「生命」——没有空气也能活，就是厌氧的；短跑喘不上气那一段也是无氧的。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ aer「空气」+ bios「生命」，由巴斯德造出法语 anaerobie，英语加 -ic 成 anaerobic，字面即「无空气而生活的」，引申指无氧运动。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one absence of oxygen: in a sealed tank of bacteria, and in a muscle working faster than the lungs can supply.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种「缺氧」：一是在密闭的细菌罐里，二是在供氧跟不上的肌肉里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life keeping going after the oxygen is pulled out
core.cn: 核心意象：氧气被抽走后生命仍在硬撑

branches.en: Black mud bubbling with methane.
branches.cn: 冒着甲烷气泡的黑泥。

branches.en: A sealed digester turning waste to gas.
branches.cn: 把废弃物变成气体的密闭消化罐。

branches.en: A forty-metre dash run on stored fuel.
branches.cn: 靠储备燃料跑完的四十米冲刺。

branches.en: A last heavy lift with held breath.
branches.cn: 憋着气完成的最后一次大重量举。

branches.en: Both run without waiting for oxygen.
branches.cn: 两者都不等氧气就运行。

intro.en: Anaerobic is an- plus aer plus bio plus -ic, and removing the prefix flips the whole meaning.
intro.cn: anaerobic 是 an- 加 aer 加 bio 加 -ic，去掉前缀就把整个意思翻过来。

latinIntro.en: All three pieces are Greek: an-, aer and bios. Pasteur assembled them in French, and English only added the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 三个部件全是希腊语：an-、aer 与 bios。巴斯德在法语中把它们组装起来，英语只加了形容词词尾。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 产生 aerobic 与 aerial。
bios 产生 biology 与 anaerobe。

definition_zh: n. （舞台后方的）背景幕；背景；（事件发生的）背景形势
definition_en: A painted cloth hung at the back of a stage; the general setting or conditions in which something happens.
core_image: 舞台最后面那块画着远山的布
scene: 谈判在通胀高企的背景下重启。 The talks resumed against a backdrop of high inflation.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：backdrop 比喻事件发生时所处的整体形势或环境。

derivatives.zh: 后面；背部
垂幕；下降
背景；出身
舞台布景；风景

senses.title: The cloth behind the stage
senses.definition: a large painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage to show the scene of the action
senses.definitionCN: 挂在舞台后部的大块彩绘布，用来显示剧情场景
senses.example: The backdrop showed a harbour at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 背景幕上画着黄昏的港口。
senses.why: Backdrop is back plus drop, a theatre word for a cloth let down from above, so it names what hangs behind.
senses.whyCN: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——drop 是剧场用语，指从上方垂下的布，因此它指挂在后面的那块。

senses.title: The setting of an event
senses.definition: the conditions or surroundings against which an event is seen and understood
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件被观看与理解时所处的条件或环境
senses.example: The reforms came against a backdrop of unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 改革是在动荡的背景下推出的。
senses.why: Once the stage picture was familiar, the word moved to the situation that stands behind any public event.
senses.whyCN: 舞台画面为人熟知之后，这个词便转指任何公共事件背后的形势。

intro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop, where drop is a theatre term for a curtain let down from the flies; the compound is recorded in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——drop 是剧场术语，指从吊景区垂下的幕；这个复合词于二十世纪初有记载。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back, the side away from the viewer.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「后面」，即背离观看者的一侧。

items.en: Old English dropa meant a drop of liquid, from the verb to fall in drops.
items.cn: 古英语 dropa 意为「一滴液体」，出自表示滴落的动词。

items.en: By the eighteenth century drop named a curtain lowered onto the stage.
items.cn: 到十八世纪 drop 指垂放到舞台上的幕布。

items.en: The compound backdrop is recorded in the 1910s for the rear painted cloth.
items.cn: 复合词 backdrop 于 1910 年代有记载，指后方的彩绘幕布。

items.en: Journalism soon used it for the conditions behind an event.
items.cn: 新闻界很快用它指事件背后的形势条件。

items.en: The phrase against a backdrop of became a standard opening in reporting.
items.cn: 「在……背景下」这一短语成为报道的标准开头之一。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the back compounds and the theatre word drop; the near-meaning group lists words for a setting.
note.cn: 形近组保留 back 复合词与剧场词 drop；近义组列出表示背景环境的词。

entries.definition: The setting, or a person’s history.
The spine or chief support.
A small bead of liquid, or a fall.
A bag carried on the back.
The surroundings of an event.
The circumstances that give meaning.
The painted structures on a stage.
The social environment of a person.

normalIntro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop, a theatre curtain let down behind the actors: then any situation standing behind an event.
normalIntro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop——垂在演员身后的剧场幕布；进而指站在事件背后的任何形势。

normal.en: The set phrase is against a backdrop of.
normal.cn: 固定短语是 against a backdrop of。

normal.en: Background is wider; backdrop is more visual.
normal.cn: background 更宽泛，backdrop 更有画面感。

normal.en: A drop is a hanging stage cloth.
normal.cn: drop 指垂挂的舞台幕布。

normal.en: It is countable: two backdrops.
normal.cn: 它可数：two backdrops。

normal.en: Scenery is built, a backdrop is hung.
normal.cn: scenery 是搭建的，backdrop 是垂挂的。

abstract.en: Picture distant hills painted on cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象布上画着的远山。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole city behind one speech.
abstract.cn: 想象一场演讲背后的整座城市。

abstract.en: Think of a frame that makes the figure readable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个让人物得以被读懂的画框。

examples.en: They rolled up the old backdrop.
examples.cn: 他们把旧背景幕卷了起来。

examples.en: The strike happened against a backdrop of cuts.
examples.cn: 罢工发生在削减开支的背景下。

examples.en: Snow peaks formed a dramatic backdrop.
examples.cn: 雪峰构成了引人注目的背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：back「后面」+ drop「垂下的幕布」——垂在舞台最后面的那块布就是 backdrop；引申为事件的背景形势。

root: 古英语 baec「后」与 dropa「滴」合成的剧场词 drop「垂幕」，在 1910 年代组成 backdrop「背景幕」；1930 年代新闻界引申为事件背景。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are what hangs behind: a painted cloth behind the actors, and a situation behind the news.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是「挂在后面的东西」：演员身后的彩绘幕布，以及新闻背后的形势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth of painted far hills at the very back of the stage
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台最后面那块画着远山的布

branches.en: A harbour painted at dusk.
branches.cn: 画着黄昏港口的幕布。

branches.en: An old cloth rolled away.
branches.cn: 被卷走的旧幕布。

branches.en: Talks held amid high prices.
branches.cn: 在高物价中举行的谈判。

branches.en: A strike set against cuts.
branches.cn: 以削减开支为背景的罢工。

branches.en: Both stand behind what is watched.
branches.cn: 两者都立于被观看之物的后方。

intro.en: Backdrop is back plus drop; the same back element builds background and backbone, while -ground gives the wider cousin.
intro.cn: backdrop 是 back 加 drop；同一 back 成分构成 background 与 backbone，而 -ground 则给出更宽泛的近亲。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native; Latin contexere, to weave together, gives context, and Latin scaena gives scene and scenery.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语；拉丁语 contexere「编织在一起」产生 context，scaena 则产生 scene 与 scenery。

definition_zh: 酗酒成瘾；酒瘾；慢性酒精中毒
definition_en: a condition in which a person cannot control drinking and suffers when it stops; also the chronic physical damage caused by years of heavy drinking
core_image: 酒杯一旦放下就浑身难受的那种依赖
scene: 他戒了三次又复发，家人已经不敢再数。 Alcoholism cost him his job and his marriage.
sceneCN: 这里 alcoholism 是「酗酒成瘾」（第 1 个义项：对酒精形成依赖、无法自控的疾病状态）；句意为酗酒让他丢了工作也毁了婚姻。核心画面是酒杯一旦放下就浑身难受的那种依赖。

pos.zh: 酗酒成瘾；酒瘾；酒精中毒

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 相关形容词，义为「酒精的；酗酒的」
去掉 -ism 的物质名词，义为「酒精；含酒精饮料」
加 non- 构成，义为「不含酒精的」

senses.title: Dependence on drinking
senses.definition: a condition in which a person cannot control drinking and suffers when it stops, treated as a disease rather than a weakness
senses.definitionCN: 一个人无法控制饮酒、停饮即出现痛苦反应的状态，被视为疾病而非意志薄弱
senses.example: Alcoholism runs in his family on both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母两边家族都有酗酒问题。
senses.why: Alcohol plus -ism names a settled condition, the same suffix that gives rheumatism and absenteeism their sense of a lasting state.
senses.whyCN: alcohol 加 -ism 表示一种固定状态，这个后缀在 rheumatism、absenteeism 中同样表示持续的状态。

senses.title: Chronic poisoning by alcohol
senses.definition: the physical damage done by years of heavy drinking, the older medical sense covering liver, nerve and brain injury
senses.definitionCN: 长年大量饮酒造成的身体损害，是较旧的医学用法，涵盖肝、神经与脑损伤
senses.example: The scan showed signs of alcoholism in the liver.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示肝脏有酒精中毒的迹象。
senses.why: Here -ism keeps its medical use of naming a morbid condition, so the word points at the damage rather than at the habit.
senses.whyCN: 这里 -ism 保留了医学上表示病态的用法，所以该词指向损害本身，而不是饮酒习惯。

intro.en: Alcoholism is alcohol plus the condition suffix -ism: the substance word came from Arabic kohl, a fine powder, and alchemists later stretched it to the spirit of wine.
intro.cn: alcoholism 是 alcohol 加表示状态的后缀 -ism：这个物质词来自阿拉伯语 kohl「细粉」，炼金术士后来把它引申为「酒的精粹」。

items.en: Arabic al-kuhl named a fine powder of antimony used to stain the eyelids, the source of kohl.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kuhl 指用于染眼睑的锑细粉，是 kohl 的来源。

items.en: Scholarly Latin alcohol kept the powder sense, then alchemists used it for any substance refined to its essence.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语 alcohol 保留细粉义，后来炼金术士用它指任何提炼到精粹的物质。

items.en: The phrase alcohol vini, the essence of wine, narrowed the word to the spirit drawn off by distillation.
items.cn: 短语 alcohol vini「酒的精粹」把该词收窄为蒸馏得到的酒精。

items.en: English took alcohol in the sixteenth century for the powder, and by the seventeenth for the active spirit in drink.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 alcohol 指细粉，到十七世纪指酒中的活性精粹。

items.en: The Swedish physician Magnus Huss coined the term in the middle of the nineteenth century to describe chronic drinking as a disease.
items.cn: 瑞典医生马格努斯·胡斯在十九世纪中叶创制该词，把长期饮酒描述为一种疾病。

items.en: Modern medicine treats alcoholism as a dependence syndrome, and the phrase alcohol use disorder is now preferred in clinics.
items.cn: 现代医学把 alcoholism 视为依赖综合征，临床上如今更常用 alcohol use disorder 这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the alcohol family; the near-meaning group lists other words for dependence and for harmful drinking.
note.cn: 形近组保留 alcohol 词族；近义组列出其他表示「依赖」与「有害饮酒」的词。

entries.definition: The intoxicating substance in drinks.
Containing alcohol, or relating to dependence on it.
entries.definitionCN: 含酒精的，或与酒精依赖有关的。

entries.definition: To treat or saturate with alcohol.
A nitrogen compound found in plants.
A compulsive dependence on a substance.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种物质的强迫性依赖。

entries.definition: The state of needing something to function.
entries.definitionCN: 需要某物才能正常运作的状态。

entries.definition: An uncontrollable craving for drink.
Lack of restraint, especially in drinking.

normalIntro.en: Alcoholism is alcohol plus -ism: the condition of being ruled by alcohol.
normalIntro.cn: alcoholism 就是 alcohol 加 -ism：被酒精支配的状态。

normal.en: -ism names a condition here, as in rheumatism, not a belief as in Buddhism.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ism 表示状态，如 rheumatism，而不是信仰，如 Buddhism 中的用法。

normal.en: Alcohol is the substance; alcoholism is the disease. One is a bottle, the other a diagnosis.
normal.cn: alcohol 是物质，alcoholism 是疾病：一个是瓶子，一个是诊断。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say treat alcoholism, not treat an alcoholism.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 treat alcoholism，不说 treat an alcoholism。

normal.en: An alcoholic is a person; alcoholism is what the person has.
normal.cn: alcoholic 指人，alcoholism 指这个人所患的病。

normal.en: Clinics now often prefer alcohol use disorder, but alcoholism remains common.
normal.cn: 临床上如今常用 alcohol use disorder，但 alcoholism 仍很普遍。

abstract.en: Picture a glass that refills itself whenever the hand puts it down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子，手一放下它就自己重新斟满。

abstract.en: Imagine a hook set in the throat that only drink can loosen.
abstract.cn: 想象喉咙里卡着一个钩子，只有酒能把它松开。

abstract.en: Think of a calendar where every crossed-out day hides a bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，每个划掉的日子背后都藏着一个酒瓶。

examples.en: He has been in recovery from alcoholism for six years.
examples.cn: 他从酒瘾中康复已有六年。

examples.en: Alcoholism is treatable, but relapse is common.
examples.cn: 酗酒可以治疗，但复发很常见。

examples.en: The clinic screens every patient for alcoholism.
examples.cn: 诊所对每位病人都做酗酒筛查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿尔可霍利曾」——阿尔可（alco）霍（hol）利曾（ism）：酒（alcohol）变成一种缠人的状态（ism），就是酗酒成瘾。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-kuhl「染眼睑的锑细粉」经中世纪拉丁语 alcohol 引申为「提炼出的精粹」，短语 alcohol vini 把它收窄为蒸馏酒精；十九世纪医学加表示病态的后缀 -ism 构成 alcoholism，字面即「酒精造成的持续病态」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses describe what alcohol does over time: one names the dependence that keeps a person drinking, the other names the physical damage that drinking leaves behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在描述酒精随时间造成的结果：一个指让人不断喝下去的依赖，一个指饮酒留下的身体损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dependence that will not let the glass go
core.cn: 核心意象：一种不肯放下酒杯的依赖

branches.en: Craving that returns each evening.
branches.cn: 每晚都会回来的渴求。

branches.en: Shaking hands when the drink stops.
branches.cn: 停饮时发抖的双手。

branches.en: A liver scarred by years of drinking.
branches.cn: 被多年饮酒损伤的肝脏。

branches.en: Nerve damage that shows in the walk.
branches.cn: 从步态上看得出的神经损伤。

branches.en: Both name a lasting condition, not one night.
branches.cn: 两者都指持续状态，而非某一个夜晚。

intro.en: Alcoholism is alcohol plus -ism, where -ism turns a substance into the lasting condition that substance produces.
intro.cn: alcoholism 是 alcohol 加 -ism，这里的 -ism 把一种物质变成它所造成的持续状态。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin alcohol first meant a fine powder and then any refined essence; the phrase alcohol vini fixed the modern sense.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alcohol 先指细粉，后指任何提炼出的精粹；短语 alcohol vini 确定了现代词义。

latinEntries.example: Alcohol first meant a powdered antimony.
The phrase narrowed alcohol to spirits.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 该短语把 alcohol 收窄为烈酒。

definition_zh: n. 水族箱，鱼缸；水族馆（复数 aquariums 或 aquaria）
definition_en: A glass tank or pool in which fish and water plants are kept alive; also the building where such tanks are shown to the public.
core_image: 一面玻璃后面，水里的世界照常运转
scene: 孩子们隔着玻璃看鳐鱼滑过。 The children watched rays glide across the aquarium.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aquarium 指养活水生物的玻璃缸或水池，也可指展出这些缸的整座场馆。

derivatives.zh: 水；水绿色
水生的；水上的
水族饲养爱好者
水产养殖

senses.title: A tank of living water
senses.definition: a glass container or small pool kept filled with water so that fish, plants and other water life can live in it
senses.definitionCN: 盛满水的玻璃容器或小池，供鱼类、水草及其他水生生物存活
senses.example: A balanced aquarium needs plants as well as fish.
senses.exampleCN: 一个平衡的水族箱既要有鱼，也要有水草。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a watering place, so the ending -arium still says place: a place made of water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原意是「饮水处」，所以词尾 -arium 仍在说「场所」：一个用水做成的场所。

senses.title: The building that shows them
senses.definition: a public institution where large tanks display sea and river life to visitors
senses.definitionCN: 用大型水箱向参观者展示海洋与河流生物的公共机构
senses.example: The city aquarium opens a jellyfish hall this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 市水族馆今春新开一个水母展厅。
senses.why: Once the tanks grew big enough to need a building, the place word stretched from the glass box to the whole hall.
senses.whyCN: 当水箱大到需要专门建筑时，这个表「场所」的词就从玻璃缸扩展到了整座展馆。

intro.en: Aquarium is Latin aquarium, a watering place for cattle, the neuter of aquarius, of water, from aqua, water. English borrowed it in 1853 for the new fish tanks.
intro.cn: aquarium 就是拉丁语 aquarium「牲畜饮水处」，是 aquarius「属于水的」的中性形式，来自 aqua「水」。英语在 1853 年借它来指新出现的鱼缸。

items.en: The reconstructed root akwa- meant water, and it also gives Old English ea, a river, seen in place names.
items.cn: 重构词根 akwa- 意为「水」，它也产生古英语 ea「河流」，保留在地名中。

items.en: Latin aqua meant water and gives aqua, aquatic, aqueduct and aquarelle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aqua 意为「水」，产生 aqua、aquatic、aqueduct 与 aquarelle。

items.en: The adjective aquarius meant of or for water, as in the water carrier of the zodiac.
items.cn: 形容词 aquarius 意为「属于水的、供水的」，如黄道十二宫中的持水者。

items.en: Its neuter form aquarium named a watering place for cattle, a place defined by its water.
items.cn: 其中性形式 aquarium 指「牲畜饮水处」，一个由水定义的场所。

items.en: In 1853 London opened a fish house and the Latin word was revived for the artificial tank.
items.cn: 1853 年伦敦开设鱼类展馆，这个拉丁词被重新起用来指人工水箱。

items.en: As tanks grew into halls, aquarium came to mean the whole public institution, not just the glass box.
items.cn: 随着水箱发展为展厅，aquarium 转而指整座公共机构，而不只是那只玻璃缸。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the water words and sets terrarium, the dry-land counterpart, beside aquarium; the near-meaning group lists other places for keeping animals.
note.cn: 形近组区分各个「水」词，并把陆生对应词 terrarium 与 aquarium 并列；近义组列出其他饲养展示动物的场所。

entries.definition: A glass case for plants or small land animals.
entries.definitionCN: 养植物或小型陆生动物的玻璃箱。

entries.definition: Rock that holds underground water.
Living or happening in water.
Water; a bluish green colour.
A container holding liquid.
A place for keeping living creatures.
A very large sea-life aquarium.
A collection of captive animals.

normalIntro.en: Aquarium is aqua, water, plus -arium, a place: a place made of water, whether a tank or a whole hall.
normalIntro.cn: aquarium 就是 aqua「水」加 -arium「场所」：用水做成的场所，小到一只缸，大到整座馆。

normal.en: Two plurals are correct: aquariums and aquaria.
normal.cn: 两种复数都对：aquariums 与 aquaria。

normal.en: Terrarium is the dry counterpart, with terra for earth.
normal.cn: terrarium 是陆生对应词，terra 意为「土」。

normal.en: Aquarium fish is a fixed pair for ornamental fish.
normal.cn: aquarium fish 是观赏鱼的固定说法。

normal.en: The stress sits on -quar-, /ˈkweə/.
normal.cn: 重音落在 -quar- 上，读 /ˈkweə/。

normal.en: The keeper is an aquarist, with -ist for a person.
normal.cn: 饲养者叫 aquarist，-ist 表人。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of river held behind glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一片被玻璃留住的河流切片。

abstract.en: Imagine a room where the walls are water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个四壁都是水的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a watering place for cattle turned into a tank.
abstract.cn: 想象牲畜饮水处变成了一只水箱。

examples.en: The aquarium keeps its coral at a steady temperature.
examples.cn: 水族馆把珊瑚养在恒定温度下。

examples.en: Both aquariums on the coast rescue injured turtles.
examples.cn: 海边这两家水族馆都救助受伤的海龟。

examples.en: The laboratory houses twelve aquaria for the study.
examples.cn: 实验室为这项研究放置了十二只水族缸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：aqua「水」+ -arium「场所」——装水的场所，小的是鱼缸，大的是水族馆 aquarium。

root: 原始印欧词根 akwa-「水」生出拉丁 aqua，形容词 aquarius「属于水的」的中性形式 aquarium 原指牲畜饮水处；1853 年英语重新起用指人工鱼缸，后扩展指水族馆。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one water place: the glass box that holds a living slice of water, and the building that holds many such boxes.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个「水的场所」：留住一片活水世界的玻璃缸，以及容纳许多这样缸的建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: behind one pane of glass, the water world keeps running
core.cn: 核心意象：一面玻璃后面，水里的世界照常运转

branches.en: A planted tank on a desk.
branches.cn: 桌上一只种了水草的缸。

branches.en: A saltwater pool for coral.
branches.cn: 养珊瑚的海水池。

branches.en: A hall of jellyfish tanks.
branches.cn: 满是水母缸的展厅。

branches.en: A city institution that rescues turtles.
branches.cn: 救助海龟的市级机构。

branches.en: Both are places defined by water.
branches.cn: 两者都是由水定义的场所。

intro.en: Aquarium is aqua plus -arium, a place suffix; the same water root builds aquatic, aquifer, aqueduct and aquaculture.
intro.cn: aquarium 是 aqua 加场所后缀 -arium；同一「水」词根还构成 aquatic、aquifer、aqueduct 与 aquaculture。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is aqua, aquarius and aquarium; terra, earth, gives the contrasting terrarium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 aqua、aquarius 与 aquarium；terra「土」给出对照词 terrarium。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aqua 是所有「水」词的开头。

latinEntries.example: Aquarium once meant a cattle trough.

definition_zh: 动机；目的；主题；动力的；推动的
definition_en: the inner force or reason that makes a person act in a certain way; also an adjective meaning causing or supplying motion
core_image: 一只手从背后推着人往某个方向走
scene: 侦探反复追问同一个问题：什么动机能让安静的邻居开三小时车去一栋空屋？ The detective kept returning to one question: what motive would make a quiet neighbour drive three hours to an empty house?
sceneCN: 这里 motive 是「作案动机」（第 2 个义项：侦查语境中驱使人行动的内在原因）；句意：探长反复回到同一个问题：什么样的动机会让一个安静的邻居开三小时车去一栋空房子？场景要点：一间堆满卷宗的办公室、一张标着三小时车程的地图、一栋没有人的房子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 动力的；推动的；引起运动的

collocations.zh: 别有用心；不可告人的动机

senses.title: The push from inside
senses.definition: the inner feeling, need, or desire that makes a person choose to act in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 使人选择以某种方式行动的内在感受、需要或欲望
senses.example: Her motive was not money but curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动机不是钱，而是好奇。
senses.why: Medieval Latin motivus meant 'moving, impelling'. The noun names the moving force inside a person, the push that starts the action before any explanation is given.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 motivus 意为“使移动、推动”。这个名词命名人内部那股推动力，即行动开始、解释尚未给出之前的那一推。

senses.title: A motive in an investigation
senses.definition: the reason a person is believed to have committed a crime or a harmful act
senses.definitionCN: 被认为促使某人实施犯罪或伤害行为的那个原因
senses.example: The police found no motive for the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 警方没有找到这次袭击的动机。
senses.why: Detectives work backwards from an act to the push that could have produced it. In that setting, motive becomes the hidden spring the whole case must locate.
senses.whyCN: 探员从行为倒推，寻找可能产生它的那一推。在这种语境里，动机变成了整个案件必须找到的那根隐藏的发条。

senses.title: A motive kept out of sight
senses.titleCN: 隐藏的、不可告人的动机
senses.definition: a real reason for acting that a person does not admit, often because it is self-interested
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不愿承认的真实动因，常因它出于私利
senses.example: He offered to help, but she suspected an ulterior motive.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出帮忙，但她怀疑他别有用心。
senses.why: If a motive is a push, it can be applied from behind, where no one sees it. The phrase 'ulterior motive' places the push out of sight, beyond the stated reason.
senses.whyCN: 如果动机是一推，它就可以从背后施加，让人看不见。“ulterior motive”这一说法把这一推放到视线之外，越过了明面上说出的理由。

senses.title: The profit motive
senses.definition: the desire for financial gain considered as the force that drives investment and business activity
senses.definitionCN: 把对经济收益的渴望看作驱动投资与商业活动的力量
senses.example: The profit motive drives most of the investment in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 利润动机驱动着这个地区的大部分投资。
senses.why: Economics turns the inner push into a system-wide force. When many people are moved by gain, the motive stops being personal and becomes the engine of a market.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把内在的一推变成整个系统的力量。当许多人被收益推动时，动机就不再是个人的，而成了市场的引擎。

senses.title: A motive behind a group act
senses.definition: the stated or suspected force behind a collective decision, such as a reform or a policy
senses.definitionCN: 集体决定背后的、被说明或被怀疑的推动力，如改革或政策
senses.example: The reform was pushed by political motives rather than by evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 推动这项改革的不是证据，而是政治动机。
senses.why: A group can be pushed too. The word then names whatever moves an assembly, party, or institution, even when no single person's feeling is involved.
senses.whyCN: 群体也会被推动。这时这个词命名的是推动一个议会、政党或机构的东西，即使其中并不涉及某一个人的感受。

senses.title: A musical motive
senses.definition: a short recurring figure or theme in a piece of music or art, often carrying a meaning
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或艺术作品中反复出现的短小音型或主题，常带有某种含义
senses.example: The three-note figure returns as a leading motive in the third act.
senses.exampleCN: 那个三音音型在第三幕作为主导动机再次出现。
senses.why: A motive in music is a small unit that keeps moving through the work, returning and developing. It is a push that carries the listener forward, which is why the same word serves both action and art.
senses.whyCN: 音乐中的动机是一个在作品中不断移动、反复出现并发展的短小单位。它是一股推着听者往前的力量，所以同一个词既用于行动，也用于艺术。

senses.title: Motive in law and morality
senses.titleCN: 法律与道德评价中的动机
senses.definition: the reason for an act as judged in law or ethics, especially when it affects how the act is evaluated
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或伦理评判中一个行为的原因，尤当它影响对该行为的评价时
senses.example: The court weighs the motive as well as the act itself.
senses.exampleCN: 法院既衡量行为本身，也衡量其动机。
senses.why: Law cares where the push came from, not only where it ended. A helping hand moved by kindness and one moved by gain produce similar acts but different judgments, so motive becomes a separate thing to assess.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心这一推从何而来，而不只是它把行为推到了哪里。出于善意的手和出于获利的手做出相似的行为，却得到不同的评判，所以动机成了需要单独评估的东西。

senses.title: Motive power
senses.definition: in the adjective use, the force that drives a machine or a process, as in 'motive power'
senses.definitionCN: 形容词用法中指驱动机器或过程的力量，如“motive power”
senses.example: Steam was the motive power of the first factories.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽是第一批工厂的动力。
senses.why: The adjective kept the literal Latin sense 'causing motion'. Steam moves an engine exactly as a desire moves a person, so the same word covers both the mental and the mechanical push.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了拉丁语字面的“引起运动”之义。蒸汽推动发动机，正如欲望推动人，所以同一个词同时覆盖心理与机械的推动。

senses.title: Motive force
senses.definition: in technical or literary use, a force that produces movement, as in 'motive force'
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或文学用法中指产生运动的力量，如“motive force”
senses.example: Gravity is the motive force behind the landslide.
senses.exampleCN: 重力是这场滑坡背后的作用力。
senses.why: Here the word is almost physics: whatever makes a body begin to move. The inner push and the physical push are the same picture seen from two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词几乎属于物理学：任何使物体开始运动的东西。内在的一推与物理的一推，是同一幅画面的两面。

intro.en: Motive comes from Medieval Latin motivus 'moving' through French, and the whole family keeps one image: something that sets a body, or a person, in motion. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: motive 经法语来自中世纪拉丁语 motivus“使移动的”，整个词族都保留同一幅画面：某物使一个身体、或一个人开始运动。年代为大致估计。

items.en: The noun first meant 'something brought forward, a proposition, assertion, or argument', a sense now obsolete. It came from Old French motif, a noun use of an adjective literally meaning 'moving'.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“被提出的东西、命题、主张或论点”，这一义项今已废弃。它来自古法语 motif，是字面意为“移动的”形容词的名词化用法。

items.en: Medieval Latin motivus meant 'moving, impelling'. It came from Latin motus 'a moving, motion', the past participle of movere 'to move'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 motivus 意为“使移动的、推动的”。它来自拉丁语 motus“移动、运动”，即 movere“移动”的过去分词。

items.en: Movere goes back to PIE *meue- 'to push away'. The same root gives motor, emotion, promote, remote, and locomotive.
items.cn: movere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *meue-“推开”。同一词根给出 motor、emotion、promote、remote 与 locomotive。

items.en: The modern sense, 'that which inwardly moves a person to behave a certain way, a mental state or force which induces an action of volition', is recorded from the early fifteenth century. Hence also 'the design or object one has in any action'.
items.cn: 现代义“在内部促使人以某种方式行动的东西，即引发意志行动的心理状态或力量”记录于 15 世纪早期。由此也引申出“任何行动中所抱的目的或对象”。

items.en: The adjective meant 'having control of motion, causing motion, having power to move someone or something'. It survives mainly in fixed phrases such as motive power and motive force.
items.cn: 形容词意为“控制运动的、引起运动的、有能力推动某人或某物的”。它主要存活于 motive power、motive force 这类固定短语中。

items.en: Motive and motivation now divide the work: motive is the inner spring itself, while motivation covers the whole process or supply of drive. Reason is the account offered for an act, and incentive is an external lure. Motivate is the verb built on motive.
items.cn: motive 与 motivation 如今分工：motive 是那根内在的发条本身，motivation 则覆盖整个激励过程或动力的供给。reason 是为行为给出的解释，incentive 是外部的诱因。motivate 是由 motive 构成的动词。

note.en: The first group separates the verb, the process noun, and the adjective built on motive; the second compares the words learners use when they mean 'why someone acted'.
note.cn: 第一组把由 motive 构成的动词、过程名词与形容词分开；第二组比较学习者表达“某人为何行动”时混用的几个词。

entries.definition: to give someone a reason or drive to act. It is the act of supplying the push, while motive is the push itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人行动的理由或动力。它是提供这一推的动作，而 motive 是这一推本身。

entries.definition: the whole process of being driven to act, or the amount of drive a person has. It is wider than motive: one motive is a specific spring, motivation is the general force or the study of it.
entries.definitionCN: 被驱动去行动的整个过程，或一个人拥有的动力总量。它比 motive 更宽：一个 motive 是一根具体的发条，motivation 是总体力量或对它的研究。

entries.definition: intended to increase someone's drive, as in a motivational speech. It describes the effect on drive, not the reason for a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 旨在增强某人干劲的，如励志演讲。它描述对干劲的效果，而不是某一次行动的原因。

entries.definition: done without any discernible reason. The -less suffix marks the absence of exactly the inner push that motive names.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何可辨原因的。 -less 后缀标记的正是 motive 所指那根内在发条的缺席。

entries.definition: the explanation a person gives for an act, or the grounds that make it intelligible. A motive is the inner push; a reason is the account laid out for others, which may or may not match the motive.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人为行为给出的解释，或使该行为可被理解的理由。motive 是内在的一推；reason 是摆给别人看的说法，它未必与动机相符。

entries.definition: something offered from outside, such as a reward, that encourages a person to act. It is the bait in front, while a motive is the push behind.
entries.definitionCN: 从外部提供、鼓励人去行动的东西，如奖励。它是前面的诱饵，而 motive 是背后的推力。

entries.definition: the result or end a person intends to bring about. Purpose looks forward to what the act is for; motive looks back to what started it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算造成的结果或终点。purpose 向前看行为为了什么；motive 向后看是什么启动了行为。

entries.definition: a sudden urge to act, often without deliberation. It is a motive at its most immediate and least reasoned.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的、常未经深思的行动冲动。它是动机最直接、最少经过推理的形态。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin movere 'to move', its participle motus, Medieval Latin motivus, and the English family motor, emotion, and motivate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 movere“移动”、它的分词 motus、中世纪拉丁语 motivus，以及英语词族 motor、emotion、motivate。

normal.en: movere means 'to move'; motivus means 'moving, impelling'. A motive is the thing that moves a person, seen from inside.
normal.cn: movere 意为“移动”，motivus 意为“使移动的、推动的”。motive 就是从内部看、推动一个人的那个东西。

normal.en: The noun first meant 'a proposition brought forward' in the late 1300s; the inner-drive sense is early 1400s.
normal.cn: 名词在 14 世纪晚期最初意为“被提出的命题”；内在驱动义要到 15 世纪早期。

normal.en: motive, motor, emotion, promote, and locomotive all contain the same 'move' root.
normal.cn: motive、motor、emotion、promote、locomotive 都含有同一个“移动”词根。

normal.en: Motivate is the act of supplying a push; motivation is the whole supply or process; motive is one particular spring.
normal.cn: motivate 是提供一推的动作；motivation 是整体的供给或过程；motive 是某一根具体的发条。

normal.en: A reason is what you say; a motive is what pushed you. The two can differ, which is why detectives distrust stated reasons.
normal.cn: reason 是你说出来的，motive 是推你的那股力。两者可以不一致，所以探员不轻信口头理由。

abstract.en: Picture a hand between someone's shoulder blades, pushing. The person moves forward, but the hand is behind and unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在某人肩胛之间向前推。人往前走了，而那只手在背后，看不见。

abstract.en: An incentive is a coin held out in front; a motive is the hand behind. A person can be led by either, or by both at once.
abstract.cn: incentive 是举在前面的一个硬币；motive 是背后的那只手。人可能被其中任何一个引导，也可能同时被两者引导。

abstract.en: In music the same push becomes a few notes that keep returning, moving the piece forward each time they sound.
abstract.cn: 在音乐里，同一股推力变成几个不断回来的音符，每次响起都把作品往前推一段。

examples.en: No one could explain the motive behind the anonymous donation.
examples.cn: 没有人能解释这笔匿名捐款背后的动机。

examples.en: The profit motive can build a railway and also abandon a town.
examples.cn: 利润动机可以修起一条铁路，也可以抛下一座城镇。

examples.en: The court found that his motive was fear, not hatred.
examples.cn: 法院认定他的动机是恐惧，而不是仇恨。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫替吾”——莫替吾拿主意，吾自有推吾向前的那股劲 → motive 动机（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 movere“移动”的派生形式 motivus“使移动的”，核心是“从背后推动人行动的那股力”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of motive, all from one hand pushing from behind: the force may be hidden or admitted, personal or collective, mental or mechanical, but it always sets something in motion.
sensesIntro.cn: motive 的九个义项都来自背后那只推动的手：这股力可以隐藏或明说，可以属于个人或群体，可以是心理的或机械的，但它总使某物开始运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a person forward from behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从背后把人向前推。

branches.en: INNER SPRING: the push is felt from inside a person, and in art the same push becomes a recurring figure that moves the work along.
branches.cn: 内在发条：这一推从人的内部被感受到；在艺术中，同一股推力变成反复出现的音型，把作品往前带。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND HUNTED: detectives search for the push behind a crime, and an ulterior motive is the same push kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 隐藏与被追查：探员寻找罪行背后的那一推，而别有用心就是同一推被藏在视线之外。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE FORCES: profit moves a market, and political motives move a reform or a party.
branches.cn: 集体力量：利润推动市场，政治动机推动改革或政党。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: law and ethics ask where the push came from, because origin changes the value of the act.
branches.cn: 评判：法律与伦理追问这一推从何而来，因为来源会改变行为的价值。

branches.en: MECHANICAL PUSH: the adjective keeps the literal sense, naming steam, gravity, or any force that starts motion.
branches.cn: 机械推动：形容词保留字面义，命名蒸汽、重力或任何使运动开始的力量。

intro.en: Motive is a Latin-derived adjective in -ive built on the 'move' stem mot-. The same stem, with e-, pro-, re-, and -or, builds emotion, promote, remote, and motor.
intro.cn: motive 是拉丁语来源、以 -ive 结尾的形容词，词干 mot- 意为“移动”。同一词干加上 e-、pro-、re- 与 -or，构成 emotion、promote、remote 与 motor。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is movere 'to move', with its participle motus and the Medieval Latin adjective motivus. The family is large because 'move' is one of the oldest and most productive ideas in the language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基是 movere“移动”，另有其分词 motus 与中世纪拉丁语形容词 motivus。这个词族庞大，因为“移动”是语言中最古老、最能产出的观念之一。

items.meaning: a moving force; an inner reason
items.meaningCN: 推动力；内在动机（mot- 移动 + -ive 形容词或名词后缀）
items.example: The motive for the trip was to see his father.
items.exampleCN: 这趟旅行的动机是去看他父亲。

items.meaning: to supply a reason or drive
items.meaningCN: 激励；促使（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Good teachers motivate students to ask questions.

items.meaning: the process or strength of being driven
items.meaningCN: 动机；积极性（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Her motivation fell after the third rejection.
items.exampleCN: 第三次被拒之后，她的积极性下降了。

items.meaningCN: 激励的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: He gives a motivational talk every Monday.
items.exampleCN: 他每周一做一次励志演讲。

items.example: The novel describes a motiveless crime.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了一桩没有动机的罪行。

items.meaning: one who or that which imparts motion
items.meaningCN: 发动机；马达（mot- 移动 + -or 施动者）
items.example: The small motor turns the fan.

items.meaning: a feeling that moves a person
items.meaningCN: 情感；情绪（e- 向外 + motion 运动）
items.example: The speech stirred a strong emotion in the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这番讲话在人群中激起强烈的情绪。

items.meaning: to move something forward; to advance
items.meaningCN: 促进；提升（pro- 向前 + mot- 移动）
items.exampleCN: 这场活动推广本地农户。

items.meaningCN: 遥远的；偏僻的（re- 向后 + mot- 移动）
items.example: They live in a remote village without a bus.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一个没有公交的偏远村庄。

items.meaning: a railway engine that moves itself
items.meaningCN: 机车；火车头（loco 从某地 + motive 移动的）
items.example: The old locomotive still runs on weekends.
items.exampleCN: 那台老机车周末仍在运行。

items.meaning: the act of moving, or an organized campaign
items.meaningCN: 移动；运动（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: A slow movement of the crowd began near the gate.
items.exampleCN: 人群在门口附近开始缓慢移动。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使移动的；推动的（motus 移动 + -ivus 形容词后缀）
移动；运动（movere 的过去分词）

definition_zh: 志向；渴望达到的目标；送气发音；吸入；抽吸；一丝气息
definition_en: a strong hope or aim to achieve something, or the act of breathing something in
core_image: 一个人站在海边深吸一口气，眼睛望着对岸还看不见的灯光
scene: 她把想去对岸读书的念头写在信的末尾，写完又对着窗外深吸了一口气。 Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
sceneCN: 这里 aspiration 指「想要达到的目标与渴望」（第 1 个义项：志向上的愿望）；句意为她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。图中可辨识物件：写满字的信纸、窗外对岸的灯光、被吸进胸腔的一口气、两次退回的信封。

pos.zh: 志向；渴望；送气音；吸入；抽吸

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，来自拉丁语「向某处呼气」，语义为「渴望、立志」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「以志向为标榜的」
由过去分词转为形容词，语义由「送气」转为「带送气的」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「追求某职位的人」

senses.title: A hoped-for aim
senses.definition: a strong hope or ambition to achieve something in the future
senses.definitionCN: 对未来取得某物所抱的强烈希望或志向
senses.example: Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant to breathe toward something, so an aspiration is a breath aimed at a distant object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此志向就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

senses.title: Longing for high rank
senses.titleCN: 对高位或大成就的渴望
senses.definition: a desire for a high position, honour or a distinguished place
senses.definitionCN: 对高职位、荣誉或显要位置的渴求
senses.example: His aspiration to the chair was known to everyone but him.
senses.exampleCN: 他想坐主席位子的心思，除了他自己，人人都知道。
senses.why: breathing toward a seat of honour is the social form of the same reach.
senses.whyCN: 朝着荣誉之位呼一口气，是同一份伸手在社会层面的形态。

senses.title: Breath released in speech
senses.definition: the audible burst of breath that follows some consonants, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 某些辅音之后可听见的一股气流，如某些词首那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: The teacher marked the aspiration after the t with a small hook.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在那个辅音之后用一个小钩标出送气。
senses.why: the phonetic sense is the literal one: breath pushed out at the moment of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 语音义是最字面的用法：说话那一刻把气推出来。

senses.title: Drawing foreign matter into the lungs
senses.definition: the entry of food, liquid or other matter into the airway and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 食物、液体或其他物质进入气道与肺部
senses.example: The nurse watched for aspiration during the night feed.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间喂食时护士一直留意有无误吸。
senses.why: here breathing in becomes dangerous because what is drawn in does not belong in the lungs.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「吸」变得危险，因为被吸进去的东西不该在肺里。

senses.title: Removal by suction
senses.definition: the use of suction to draw fluid or tissue out of a cavity
senses.definitionCN: 用负压把液体或组织从腔体中吸出
senses.example: The aspiration of the cyst took less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 囊肿的抽吸不到一分钟就完成了。
senses.why: the same drawing motion is turned to medical use, where breath is replaced by a pump.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「吸」的动作被转作医疗用途，只是呼气换成了泵。

senses.title: Drawing fluid up a tube
senses.definition: the lifting of liquid by reduced pressure in an engine, pump or laboratory line
senses.definitionCN: 在发动机、泵或实验管路中借压差把液体吸上来
senses.example: Fuel aspiration failed when the line cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 管路开裂后燃油抽吸失效。
senses.why: machines borrow the word because a pump also pulls matter toward itself by creating a void.
senses.whyCN: 机器借用这个词，因为泵也靠制造空处把物质拉向自己。

senses.title: A breath of air
senses.definition: a single breath or a faint movement of air
senses.definitionCN: 一次呼吸，或空气极轻微的流动
senses.example: An aspiration of wind came through the shutter and moved the ash.
senses.exampleCN: 一丝风从百叶窗里进来，吹动了灰。
senses.why: the oldest physical layer survives in literary use, where the word means the air itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理层在文学用法里留存，那里这个词指空气本身。

senses.title: Shared hopes of a group
senses.definition: the collective hopes that a community or a generation holds for its future
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群或一代人对自身未来所抱的共同希望
senses.example: The school was built on the aspirations of families who had never had one.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校建立于那些从未有过学校的家庭的期盼之上。
senses.why: many breaths aimed at one future add up to a public aspiration, which is how politics uses the word.
senses.whyCN: 许多口气朝同一个未来呼出，就汇成一种公共期盼，政治语言正是这样用它的。

intro.en: Aspiration comes from Latin aspiratio 'a breathing upon', from aspirare 'to breathe toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspiratio「朝某物呼气」，其动词 aspirare「向……呼气」由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the comparison with a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相比对，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', and by metaphor to favour or to strive toward.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，并比喻为「眷顾」或「向往」。

items.en: The noun aspiratio named the breathing and, in grammar, the rough breathing marked over certain letters.
items.cn: 名词 aspiratio 指这股呼气，并在语法中指标在某些字母上的粗气符号。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, first for the grammatical sense of rough breathing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个名词，最早用于语法上的「粗气」义。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was used for a hope directed at a high aim, and the medical suction sense followed in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词用于指向高目标的希望；医学上的抽吸义在十九世纪随后出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes the first use for ambition, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住它首次用于「抱负」的时间；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built on the breathing verb from words that only sound similar; group two separates kinds of longing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的形近词与只是读音相近的词；第二组区分不同类型的渴望。

entries.definition: To aim at something high; the noun is the state, the verb is the reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 朝高处立志；名词是那个状态，动词是那次伸手。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: a breathing in, hence the sudden idea that seems to arrive from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：吸进来，因而指仿佛从外面到来的灵感。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: breathing out, and by extension the end of a period when time has run out.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出，并引申指期限走完的到期。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus spirare: the whole cycle of breathing, with no aim attached.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re-「再」加 spirare 构成：整个呼吸循环，不含目标。

entries.definition: From the same sprinkling verb, but it means a casting of doubt or a slander, not a hope.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「洒、喷」的动词，但意思是对人泼脏水、造谣中伤，而非希望。

entries.definition: A strong desire to rise in status or power; it is more worldly than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 对地位或权力上升的强烈欲望；比 aspiration 更世俗。

entries.definition: A specific end point one works toward; it is the target itself, not the longing for it.
entries.definitionCN: 努力所指向的具体终点；是目标本身，而不是对目标的渴望。

entries.definition: A cherished wish, often distant and not yet planned; it is warmer and looser than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 珍爱的愿望，往往遥远且尚无计划；比 aspiration 更温暖也更松散。

entries.definition: A deep and often painful longing; it stresses the ache rather than the plan to achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 深沉而常带痛感的渴望；强调那份渴，而不是实现它的计划。

entries.definition: The amount taken into the body or a machine in a period; it is the plain physical relative of the suction sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入身体或机器的量；是抽吸义最朴素的物理近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so a strong hope is a breath aimed at a far target.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此一份强烈的希望就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspirational, aspirated.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、追求者、愿景式形容词与送气形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: career aspirations, aspiration pneumonia, aspirated consonant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：职业志向、吸入性肺炎、送气辅音。

normal.en: The same breathing verb gives inspiration, expiration and respiration, each with its own prefix direction.
normal.cn: 同一个「呼吸」动词还给出 inspiration、expiration 与 respiration，各自带有自己的前缀方向。

normal.en: Medical suction keeps the physical picture: something is drawn out of a cavity by reduced pressure.
normal.cn: 医学抽吸保留了物理图景：靠压差把某物从腔体中吸出。

abstract.en: Picture a long breath held while looking across water at lights not yet reachable.
abstract.cn: 想象隔水望着还够不到的灯光时，长长地屏住一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a seed on a sill, leaning toward a window it cannot move to.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上的一粒种子，朝它无法移动过去的窗子倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a letter written and rewritten but never sent, kept in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一封写了又改、始终没寄出的信，放在抽屉里。

examples.en: The scholarship matched her aspiration with a place at the college.
examples.cn: 这笔奖学金让她的志向与一个学院名额对上了。

examples.en: Rural families spoke of their aspirations for a clinic of their own.
examples.cn: 乡下家庭谈起他们想要一所自己的诊所的期盼。

examples.en: The doctor ordered suction to prevent aspiration during sleep.
examples.cn: 医生安排了吸痰，以防睡眠中误吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯匹瑞」——朝远处深吸一口气再向前望 → 志向、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspiratio「呼气」← aspirare「向……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: air is aimed at a far object and becomes a hope; the same air is aimed at a seat of honour, then at a consonant, then drawn into a lung, then pulled by a pump, then felt as a faint wind, and finally shared by a whole community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：气朝远处目标呼出而成希望；同一口气再朝荣誉之位、朝一个辅音、进一只肺、被泵抽动、化作一丝风，最后被整个社群共同呼出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long breath drawn at the shore while looking at lights across the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在岸边望着对岸的灯光，长长吸一口气。

branches.en: THE BREATH AIMED HIGH: hope for an aim and hunger for a seat of honour.
branches.cn: 朝高处呼出的气：对目标的希望，以及对荣誉之位的渴求。

branches.en: THE BREATH HEARD: phonetics keeps the literal push of air.
branches.cn: 被听见的气：语音学保留了最字面的推气。

branches.en: MATTER DRAWN IN: what enters a lung and what a pump pulls up a line.
branches.cn: 被吸进的物质：进入肺里的东西，与泵沿着管路抽上来的东西。

branches.en: MATTER TAKEN OUT: clinical suction reverses the direction and removes.
branches.cn: 被取出的物质：临床抽吸把方向反过来，取走东西。

branches.en: FROM A GUST TO A GENERATION: one faint breath widens into the shared hopes of many.
branches.cn: 从一阵微风到一代人：一丝微弱的气，扩展成许多人的共同期盼。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb plus a noun suffix, and the same prefix and verb build several common English words, so the family is easy to read by parts.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加名词后缀，同一个前缀与动词还构成若干常用英语词，因此这一族很容易按部件读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adjacent and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adjacent 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix points the breath at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把气指向某个对象。
这个词根带着呼吸这个动作。

items.example: The wind seemed to strive toward the cliff.
items.exampleCN: 那阵风仿佛朝崖上使劲。

items.example: Her aspiration was to build a clinic.
items.exampleCN: 她的志向是建一所诊所。

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: He aspired to the vacant chair.
items.exampleCN: 他渴望那把空出的椅子。
十名求职者参加了考试。

items.example: The poster was aspirational rather than factual.
items.exampleCN: 这张海报是励志的，而不是写实的。

items.meaning: pronounced with a burst of breath
items.example: The aspirated consonant was hard for the children.
items.exampleCN: 这个送气辅音让孩子们觉得难。

items.meaning: a breathing in, a sudden idea
items.example: The design came in a single inspiration.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计来自一次顿悟。

items.meaning: breathing out, the end of a term
items.example: The lease reached expiration in June.
The spirit of the place was quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个地方的气息很安静。
